findings.severity: high - removes the entire class of typo/drift bugs between the lifecycle layer and the wire contract, and lets the type checker prove every terminal_reason on the wire is a member of the closed set the UI branches on
findings.title: terminal_reason is a free `str | None` on the wire although a canonical `TerminalReason` Literal already exists internally
findings.description: `terminal_reason: str | None` appears on five status/metrics response models. The codebase ALREADY defines the closed vocabulary as `TerminalReason = Literal['completed','superseded','timed_out','cancelled','memory_limited','contract_error','error']` in src/haute/routes/_job_lifecycle.py:24-32, with a `TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS` mapping (line 34) and a precedence table (line 48) keyed on exactly those literals. Producers set these values from that closed set (e.g. _optimiser_service.py:329 `terminal_reason='memory_limited'`, :2855 `'contract_error'`; _worker_isolation.py:107/131/142). Because the wire field is `str`, the contract does not express the invariant `terminal_reason in TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS`; a producer or test that emits a misspelled reason (e.g. 'memory_limit' vs 'memory_limited') type-checks and serialises fine, and the frontend silently falls through its switch. The `JobStatus` field on these same models IS a Literal, so the asymmetry is striking: status is closed but the reason that DERIVES the status is open.
findings.recommended_design: Move `TerminalReason` (the Literal) into schemas.py (or import it there so it is the single source of truth shared with _job_lifecycle.py), and change every `terminal_reason: str | None` to `terminal_reason: TerminalReason | None`. Then `JobStatus` can be derived as `JobStatus = Literal['running'] | TerminalReason`-equivalent (see separate finding) so the two sets can never drift. This makes the lifecycle layer's `TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS` mapping total-by-construction over the wire type.

findings.severity: high - eliminates a hand-maintained duplicate-literal-set that must be kept in sync across two modules; a divergence today is only caught (if at all) by runtime KeyError, not by the type system
findings.title: JobStatus and TerminalReason are two independently-authored literal sets that must agree by hand
findings.description: schemas.py defines `JobStatus = Literal['running','completed','error','cancelled','superseded','timed_out','memory_limited','contract_error']` (8 members). _job_lifecycle.py independently defines `TerminalReason` (7 members) and derives `JOB_STATUSES = frozenset({RUNNING_STATUS, *TERMINAL_STATUSES})` (line 45) plus a per-status string constant for each (lines 15-22). The intended invariant is exactly `JobStatus == {'running'} ∪ TerminalReason`, but nothing enforces it: the two literal lists are typed out by hand in different files. If someone adds a new terminal reason (say 'evicted') to TerminalReason and the mapping, `JobStatus` will not include it, so `ExploreStatusResponse(status='evicted')` raises a Pydantic validation error at the boundary that the type checker could not foresee — and conversely a value added only to JobStatus is unreachable. `_job_lifecycle.py:13` already imports `JobStatus` from schemas, so the dependency edge exists; the relationship is just not expressed structurally.
findings.recommended_design: Express the union at the type level so it cannot drift: define `TerminalReason` once (the canonical 7-member Literal), then `JobStatus = Literal['running'] | TerminalReason` using `typing.Literal` composition (or `TerminalReason` plus an explicit `RunningStatus = Literal['running']` and `JobStatus = RunningStatus | TerminalReason`). Keep both in schemas.py and import into _job_lifecycle.py. Add a one-line static assertion test `set(get_args(JobStatus)) == {'running'} | set(get_args(TerminalReason))` so any future edit to one is forced to update the other.

findings.severity: medium - NodeResult.status is consumed by `== 'error'` / `== 'ok'` comparisons in at least four modules; an enum/Literal makes those comparisons exhaustively checkable and prevents a producer from emitting an out-of-band status
findings.title: NodeResult.status is a free `str` though it is a closed two-value set consumed by equality checks
findings.description: `NodeResult.status: str` (a required field, no default). Every producer sets it to exactly 'ok' or 'error' (executor.py:1168/1190/1200/1228), and consumers branch on those exact strings: executor.py:1249 `r.status == 'error'`, cli/_run.py:63 `res.status == 'ok'`, _scaffold.py:1213 `res.status != 'ok'`, routes/pipeline.py:608 builds `node_statuses` from `r.status`. Because the field is `str`, a refactor that introduced a third state ('skipped', 'partial') or a typo ('erro') would compile and serialise, and the downstream `== 'error'` checks would silently treat it as success. This is the same closed-set pattern the file already models correctly elsewhere with Literal (e.g. ExploreRunResponse.status, TrainResponse.status).
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `NodeStatus = Literal['ok', 'error']` and type `NodeResult.status: NodeStatus`. Update `PreviewNodeResponse.node_statuses: dict[str, str]` (line 284) to `dict[str, NodeStatus]` so the per-node status map is equally closed. The equality-check sites then become statically exhaustive (mypy can flag a missed branch via assert_never).

findings.severity: medium - small closed set ('missing'|'stale') produced in exactly two places; a Literal makes the two-value contract explicit and lets the UI switch be checked
findings.title: SchemaWarning.status is a free `str` for a two-value enum ('missing' | 'stale')
findings.description: `SchemaWarning.status: str`. The only producers are executor.py:1124 `SchemaWarning(column=c, status='missing')` and executor.py:1160 `status='stale'`. The field name `status` overloaded as a *warning kind* is itself slightly misleading, but the concrete defect is that the closed set {'missing','stale'} is typed as open `str`. The frontend renders different affordances per kind; an unmodelled third value would render as nothing. Contrast `ExploreDataQualityIssue.severity: Literal['warning','danger']` (line 429) in the same file, which models its closed kind correctly.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `SchemaWarningKind = Literal['missing', 'stale']` and type `SchemaWarning.status: SchemaWarningKind` (consider renaming the field to `kind` in a coordinated frontend change, but the Literal is the load-bearing fix). NodeResult.schema_warnings and the three node_schema_warnings maps then carry the closed kind automatically.

findings.severity: medium - three adjacent closed-set fields modelled as open str; makes the diagnostic contract self-describing and lets the UI exhaustively branch on code/severity
findings.title: TraceCorrelationDiagnosticResponse.code / severity / match_strategy are free `str` for closed sets
findings.description: Three fields on this diagnostic model are stringly-typed: `code: str`, `severity: str`, `match_strategy: str`. The producer (_trace_correlation.py:211-223) emits a single fixed `code='ambiguous_row_match'` and `severity='warning'`; `match_strategy` is sourced from _trace_correlation.py:308 `'relaxed'` / :363 `'exact'`. So in practice code∈{'ambiguous_row_match'}, severity∈{'warning','danger'} (the file's own ExploreDataQualityIssue uses exactly that severity pair), and match_strategy∈{'relaxed','exact'}. As written, the wire contract cannot tell a client which codes exist, and a typo'd severity would defeat any UI colour-coding silently. The sibling severity field elsewhere in the same file is already a Literal, so this is an internal inconsistency.
findings.recommended_design: Add `TraceDiagnosticCode = Literal['ambiguous_row_match']` (extend as new diagnostics appear), reuse a shared `DiagnosticSeverity = Literal['warning','danger']` (factor it out of ExploreDataQualityIssue so both share one definition), and `MatchStrategy = Literal['exact','relaxed']`. Type the three fields accordingly. Also reuse `MatchStrategy` for any other match_strategy field.

findings.severity: medium - 'online'|'ratebook' is a pervasively-branched closed set; a Literal prevents an unmodelled mode from flowing to the apply/score path
findings.title: OptimiserSolveResult.mode is `str | None` for the closed 'online' | 'ratebook' set
findings.description: `OptimiserSolveResult.mode: str | None`. Across the optimiser/builders code, `mode` is exhaustively branched as the two-value set 'online'|'ratebook': _builders.py:1383 `!= 'ratebook'`, projection.py:696 `== 'ratebook'`, _optimiser_service.py:552/2351('online')/2501('ratebook'), optimiser.py:1571 `== 'ratebook'`. The default is always 'online'. Modelling this as open `str | None` on the wire means a serialised result could carry an unmodelled mode and the consuming ratebook/online branches would silently take the else-path. The optional `None` additionally overlaps semantically with the 'online' default — two representations of effectively the same state (mild illegal-states smell).
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `OptimiserMode = Literal['online', 'ratebook']` and type `mode: OptimiserMode | None` (or, if a mode is always known by the time a result exists, make it required `OptimiserMode` and drop the None to collapse the redundant null/'online' duplication). Reuse the same `OptimiserMode` alias anywhere the optimiser config mode is surfaced.

findings.severity: medium - 8-value documented closed set typed as open str; additionally the channel is overloaded to carry error strings, mixing a value-enum with an error message
findings.title: row_lineage_type is `str | None` for a documented 8-value closed set, and the same field doubles as an error-message carrier
findings.description: `TraceStepResponse.row_lineage_type: str | None`. The producer `detect_row_lineage_type` (_trace_enrichment.py:870) documents and returns exactly one of {'created','selected','filtered','aggregated','joined','expanded','sorted','passthrough'} (return type annotated merely `str`). Two defects: (a) stringly-typed — the closed lineage vocabulary is not on the type; the trace UI keys colour/iconography on these strings and an unmodelled value renders blank. (b) illegal-states overloading — _trace_enrichment.py:1815 assigns `step.row_lineage_type = f'error: row lineage detection failed: {exc}'`, so the SAME field that is supposed to hold a member of the enum can instead hold a free-form error string. A consumer cannot distinguish 'a lineage value' from 'an error sentinel' except by string-prefix sniffing 'error:'.
findings.recommended_design: Define `RowLineageType = Literal['created','selected','filtered','aggregated','joined','expanded','sorted','passthrough']`, annotate both `detect_row_lineage_type` -> RowLineageType and the field `row_lineage_type: RowLineageType | None`. Carry the detection failure in a separate optional field (e.g. `row_lineage_error: str | None`) rather than poisoning the enum field, so 'value' and 'error' become unrepresentable simultaneously in the wrong slot.

findings.severity: medium - closed 3-value set documented in inline comments in 3+ files but never typed; consumers compare with `== 'holdout'`
findings.title: diagnostics_set is a free `str` whose closed set ('train'|'validation'|'holdout') is only documented in comments
findings.description: `TrainResponse.diagnostics_set: str = 'validation'` with an inline comment `# 'train' | 'validation' | 'holdout'`. The identical comment-documented-but-untyped pattern repeats at modelling/_result_types.py:30 and modelling/_training_job.py:181 & :249. Producers assign from a closed set (_training_job.py:1117 'holdout', :1120 'validation', :1123 'train') and consumers branch on it: _model_card.py:111 `diag.diagnostics_set != 'holdout'`. The three legal values are effectively an enum; encoding them as `str` lets a typo flow to the model card and silently change which header/metrics block renders.
findings.recommended_design: Define `DiagnosticsSet = Literal['train', 'validation', 'holdout']` once and use it for the wire field and for the internal dataclasses in modelling/_result_types.py and _training_job.py (replacing the three duplicated explanatory comments with the type). The `!= 'holdout'` comparison then becomes statically meaningful.

findings.severity: low - closed 4-value set produced by one module; a Literal documents the policy taxonomy and prevents drift
findings.title: budget_policy is a free `str` for the closed set {'fixed_default','explicit_env','adaptive_local'}
findings.description: `ExecutionAdmissionPayload.budget_policy: str = 'fixed_default'` and `ExecutionMemoryPressureEventPayload.budget_policy: str | None = None`. The producer enumerates the closed taxonomy in _execution_admission.py: 'explicit_env' (line 310), 'adaptive_local' (line 324), 'fixed_default' (line 334), and the dataclass default 'fixed_default' (line 220). These are the only values that ever occur. Modelling as `str` means the policy vocabulary is invisible in the contract and a new policy could be emitted without the schema (or any dashboard parsing it) being updated.
findings.recommended_design: Define `BudgetPolicy = Literal['fixed_default', 'explicit_env', 'adaptive_local']` and use it for both payload fields and the internal _execution_admission dataclass field (budget_policy at lines 220/229). The two wire models then share one source of truth with the producer.

findings.severity: medium - a 0..1 fraction with no bound permits NaN/inf/negative/>1 values to cross the wire and reach progress bars; a constrained float makes the invariant unrepresentable-if-violated and is consistent with the file's own bounded-int fields
findings.title: progress is an unconstrained `float` despite being a 0.0..1.0 fraction
findings.description: Four status models declare `progress: float = 0.0`. Producers feed it fractional values (e.g. _explore_service.py:773 `progress=0.1`, :792 `progress=0.85`) and the UI renders it as a 0..100% bar. There is no `ge=0, le=1` constraint, so a buggy producer (or a job-store dict that was never coerced — values come via `job.get('progress', 0.0)` at modelling.py:111, optimiser.py:1230, etc.) can emit a negative, >1, NaN, or inf progress and Pydantic will happily serialise it, overflowing or NaN-poisoning the progress bar. The file already constrains other bounded numerics (PreviewNodeRequest.row_limit `ge=1, le=10000`, StreamingChunkSize `ge=1`, OptimiserFrontierRequest.n_points_per_dim `ge=1, le=100`), so leaving the progress fraction unbounded is an inconsistency.
findings.recommended_design: Define a shared `Progress = Annotated[float, Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False)]` and use it for all four progress fields (and `OptimiserHistoryEntry`/other 0..1 ratio fields where applicable). This makes an out-of-range progress unrepresentable on the wire and forces producers to clamp at the source.

findings.severity: medium - the response-side range model permits min>max and NaN/inf bounds even though the request side rigorously rejects them via the shared _normalise_frontier_range_pair; the invariant is enforced on input but not on the value's own type
findings.title: OptimiserFrontierRange allows min > max and non-finite bounds (the request path validates this, the response model does not)
findings.description: `OptimiserFrontierRange` is `{min: float, max: float}` with no validator. The request side enforces the full invariant (finite, min<=max) via `_normalise_frontier_range_pair` (schemas.py:45-69) wired into `OptimiserFrontierRequest._validate_threshold_ranges`. But the response/auto-range model `OptimiserFrontierRange` re-declares the same min/max pair WITHOUT any guard, and is constructed directly from a producer dict (_optimiser_service.py:3542 `OptimiserFrontierRange(min=value['min'], max=value['max'])`, :3833 likewise) that is not routed through the canonical validator. So a degenerate or inverted range (min>max, or NaN bounds) is representable in the response and flows to the frontier UI, which assumes a well-ordered finite interval. The ordering invariant is a property of the *value*, so it belongs on the type, not only on one entry path.
findings.recommended_design: Attach a `@model_validator(mode='after')` to OptimiserFrontierRange that calls the existing `_normalise_frontier_range_pair((min,max), field='range')` (reusing the single source of truth) to assert finiteness and min<=max — making an ill-formed range unconstructable regardless of which path builds it. Optionally encode bounds as `Annotated[float, Field(allow_inf_nan=False)]` to cover the finiteness half at the field level.

findings.severity: low - small closed set ('parquet'|'csv') the codegen already hardcodes; a Literal documents the supported sink formats
findings.title: SinkResponse.format is a free `str` defaulting to 'parquet' for a known closed set
findings.description: `SinkResponse.format: str = 'parquet'`. The sink codegen only ever emits two formats — _codegen_builders.py:372 `format='parquet'` and :382 `format='csv'` — and executor.py:1566/1589 logs/sets the format from that same closed choice. The wire field being open `str` hides the supported-format set from clients and would let an unsupported format value be reported without any type-level signal.
findings.recommended_design: Define `SinkFormat = Literal['parquet', 'csv']` and type `SinkResponse.format: SinkFormat`. Reuse the alias at the codegen/executor sink sites so the supported-format list has one definition.

findings.location: src/haute/schemas.py:86-94 (SavePipelineRequest.sources:93, active_source:94, source default at PreviewNodeRequest.source:256 etc.)
findings.type_name: SavePipelineRequest (sources / active_source) and the pervasive `source` field
findings.severity: low - the active_source ∈ sources invariant is left unchecked; an inconsistent pair (active_source not in sources) is representable and would later fail deep in execution rather than at the boundary
findings.title: SavePipelineRequest.active_source is not constrained to be a member of sources (cross-field invariant unmodelled)
findings.description: `SavePipelineRequest` has `sources: list[str] = ['live']` and `active_source: str = 'live'` as two independent fields. The implicit invariant is `active_source in sources`, but nothing enforces it, so a payload with `sources=['live','prod']` and `active_source='staging'` is accepted and only fails (if at all) later when execution tries to resolve the active source. More broadly, `source` is a free `str` defaulting to 'live' on ~10 request models (PreviewNodeRequest:256, TraceRequest:305, SinkRequest:371, ExploreRunRequest:468, TrainRequest:822, OptimiserEstimateRequest:1021, ...); the set of valid sources is dynamic so a Literal is not appropriate, but the cross-field membership invariant for the save request is checkable at the boundary.
findings.recommended_design: Add a `@model_validator(mode='after')` on SavePipelineRequest asserting `active_source in sources` (and `sources` non-empty), turning an inconsistent source selection into a 422 at the contract boundary instead of a deferred runtime failure. Consider a `SourceName = NewType('SourceName', str)` alias to document the otherwise-bare `source` strings, even though their domain stays open.

findings.location: src/haute/_api_input_schema.py:107-142 (ColumnV2, TableV2, ApiInputV2Config TypedDicts) consumed by validate_v2_schema at :263-403
findings.severity: medium - the entire v2 schema contract is a `total=False` TypedDict whose every invariant (required label/path/name, allowed type, unique labels, levels-non-empty, row_id membership) is re-checked by hand in a 140-line imperative validator; required-ness and the ColumnType/ColumnStatus enums are declared on the TypedDict but the all-optional shape means the type system proves none of them
findings.title: v2 schema is an all-optional TypedDict with every invariant enforced by a hand-written validator instead of the type
findings.description: `ColumnV2`, `TableV2`, and `ApiInputV2Config` are `TypedDict(total=False)`, so EVERY field is optional at the type level — `name`, `path`, `label`, `type`, `status` all included. The real contract (validate_v2_schema, lines 263-403) requires `label` (non-empty str), `path` (parseable), each column's `name` (non-empty, unique) and `path` (under table path) and `type` ∈ allowed set, plus `levels` non-empty-if-present and `row_id_column` membership. None of these are expressed by the TypedDict: a `ColumnV2` literal missing `name`/`type`, or with `type='date'` mistyped, type-checks fine; the 140 lines of `isinstance(...)` / `not ... or ...` re-assert at runtime what a stricter model could guarantee. Note the field-level enums ARE declared (`type: ColumnType`, `status: ColumnStatus` at lines 110/111, with ColumnType/ColumnStatus Literals at 64-65) — good — but `total=False` makes them non-binding, and the `_ALLOWED_COLUMN_TYPES` frozenset (line 67) duplicates `ColumnType`'s members as a parallel runtime constant that must be kept in sync by hand.
findings.recommended_design: Promote the v2 schema to a Pydantic model hierarchy (ColumnV2Model, TableV2Model, ApiInputV2ConfigModel) with required fields required (`name: str`, `path: str`, `label: str`, `type: ColumnType`, `status: ColumnStatus`), field validators for the path-shape checks (parse_table_path/parse_column_path), and model validators for the cross-field invariants (unique labels, sanitised-label collision/B2, unique column names, levels-non-empty, row_id_column ∈ column names). Derive `_ALLOWED_COLUMN_TYPES` from `get_args(ColumnType)` instead of duplicating the literal set. This collapses the imperative validator into declarative constraints and makes an invalid schema largely unconstructable; keep ApiInputSchemaError only for the genuinely cross-table checks Pydantic can't express, raised from a model_validator.

findings.location: src/haute/schemas.py:680-695 (JsonCacheBuildResponse: row_count:683, column_count:684, size_bytes:686, skipped_records:694) and the many `*_bytes`/`*_count`/`row_count` ints across the file
findings.type_name: JsonCacheBuildResponse and peer payloads (count/byte integer fields)
findings.severity: low - dozens of non-negative quantities (row_count, column_count, *_bytes, *_count, skipped_records) are unconstrained ints; a negative value is representable and meaningless, though producers are unlikely to emit one
findings.title: Non-negative count/byte integer fields are unconstrained `int` (negatives representable)
findings.description: Quantity fields that are physically non-negative are typed as bare `int`, e.g. JsonCacheBuildResponse.row_count/column_count/size_bytes/cached_at and skipped_records (694), NodeResult.row_count/column_count/memory_bytes, FetchTableResponse.row_count/column_count/size_bytes, and the ExecutionMetricsPayload rss_*_bytes family. None carry `ge=0`. A negative row_count or size_bytes is a nonsense state that the contract nonetheless permits; it would silently propagate to UI summations and percentage math. This is the same omission class as the unbounded `progress` finding but lower severity because producers derive these from len()/os.stat and are unlikely to go negative — still, the type does not encode the invariant.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `NonNegativeInt = Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]` (or use pydantic's `NonNegativeInt`) and apply it to the count/byte/row fields across the response models. This is a mechanical, low-risk tightening that makes negative quantities unrepresentable and documents the domain. Apply the same to the few non-negative floats (elapsed_ms, size in seconds) via `Field(ge=0)`.

findings.severity: low - clustered booleans (is_main/is_read_only; is_yours/is_current/is_archived) admit contradictory combinations the domain forbids; modest bug-surface, mainly a clarity/illegal-state observation
findings.title: Git status/branch boolean clusters permit contradictory flag combinations
findings.description: GitStatusResponse carries `is_main: bool` and `is_read_only: bool` as independent flags; GitBranchItem carries `is_yours/is_current/is_archived` as three independent bools. Some combinations are domain-contradictions (e.g. a branch that is both `is_current=True` and `is_archived=True`, or main-detection flags that disagree with the branch name). Independent booleans make those illegal combinations representable. This is a milder instance of the boolean-blindness anti-pattern; the read-only/main relationship in particular is a derived fact, not two free inputs.
findings.recommended_design: Where a cluster is mutually exclusive, model it as a single Literal/enum (e.g. branch lifecycle `Literal['active','archived']` instead of `is_archived`, and `is_current` derived against the response's `current` field rather than stored). For is_read_only as a function of is_main, consider computing it via a `@computed_field` so the relationship can't be set inconsistently. Lower priority than the status/enum findings but removes a representable-contradiction class.

results.coverage_note: Read both target files IN FULL (schemas.py 1347 lines; _api_input_schema.py 403 lines) and cross-checked producers/consumers across executor.py, routes/*, _job_lifecycle.py, _trace_correlation.py, _trace_enrichment.py, _execution_admission.py, _codegen_builders.py, modelling/_training_job.py and _result_types.py to verify each closed-set claim against real call sites. Dedup check performed against review/02-findings/catalog.md and review/04-exhaustive/EXHAUSTIVE-FINDINGS.md + review/05-dimensions/raw/*: the existing findings on these files are RUNTIME bugs (float() coercion messages B020; bool-as-range-bound B020; parse_column_path array-crossing B056; row_id_column unselected-membership B056; volatile_schema:Any 422-bypass) and a row_count/preview default mismatch — none overlap the TYPE/INVARIANT design issues reported here. Key reusable discovery for remediation: a canonical `TerminalReason` Literal + `TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS` mapping + `JOB_STATUSES` ALREADY exist in src/haute/routes/_job_lifecycle.py:24-45, so the terminal_reason/JobStatus findings are about importing/sharing an existing closed set rather than inventing one. Types already WELL-DESIGNED (called out so they are not 'fixed'): ExecutionMemoryPressureEventPayload.event (Literal['memory_pressure']), ExecutionMemoryLimitErrorPayload.error_code (Literal['memory_limit']), ExploreColumnKind, ExploreRunResponse.status / ExploreCacheReport.status, ExploreDataQualityIssue.severity (Literal['warning','danger']), TrainResponse.status, MlflowLogResponse.status, all *Solve/*Apply Literal status starts, the StreamingChunkSize bool-reject + ge/le Annotated alias, and the bounded row_limit/n_points_per_dim Fields — these demonstrate the codebase knows the pattern, which makes the remaining free-str status/mode/type fields true inconsistencies rather than a uniform style. Confidence is high on the stringly-typed enum findings (each closed set verified at its producer) and medium on the structural promotions (TypedDict->Pydantic, OptimiserFrontierRange validator, cross-field active_source) where the change is larger.

findings.severity: high
findings.title: PipelineGraph permits a nodes list with duplicate ids; node_map silently collapses them (uniqueness is not a type invariant)
findings.description: PipelineGraph.nodes is a plain `list[GraphNode]` with no model_validator enforcing id-uniqueness. The canonical `node_map` is built as `{n.id: n for n in self.nodes}` (line 700), which silently drops all but the last node sharing an id, and `parents_of`/topo/cache-key code all assume `node_map` is a total bijection over `nodes`. So a `PipelineGraph` where two GraphNodes share an id is a representable-but-illegal state: every id-keyed lookup (executor node_map, projection, fingerprint, deploy) operates on a different node-set than `len(graph.nodes)` implies. The existing finding `duplicate-func-name-node-collapse` (review/02-findings/findings.json:900) documents the PARSER symptom and proposes a parser-layer guard; this is the distinct TYPE-LEVEL root cause: the canonical graph type itself accepts the collision, so any producer (parser, submodel merge, route edits, programmatic construction) can reintroduce it. Promoting uniqueness to a constructor invariant makes node_map total-by-construction and closes the class, not one instance.
findings.recommended_design: Add a Pydantic `@model_validator(mode="after")` on PipelineGraph that raises if `len({n.id for n in self.nodes}) != len(self.nodes)`, naming the duplicate ids. This makes the collapse unconstructable and lets node_map/parents_of/fingerprint code rely on `nodes` and `node_map` having identical cardinality. (Independently, the parser should be fixed per the existing behavioral finding; the type invariant is the backstop guaranteeing no other code path can recreate it.)
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Removes an entire class of silent node-loss across executor, codegen, projection and deploy — any path that mutates the node list is currently unguarded.

findings.severity: high
findings.title: active_source not constrained to be a member of sources on PipelineGraph, though the identical invariant IS enforced on SidecarModel
findings.description: PipelineGraph declares `sources: list[str] = ["live"]` and `active_source: str = "live"` with no validator tying them together, so `PipelineGraph(sources=["live"], active_source="test")` is constructible. The SAME pair of fields on SidecarModel (routes/_helpers.py:62) carries a `@model_validator` `_active_source_must_be_in_sources` that raises when `active_source not in sources`. The canonical graph type — which is what codegen (codegen.py:954/1090/1252), the dataframe cache (_dataframe_execution_cache.py:230-231) and the save path (_save_pipeline.py:866-867) actually read — has no such guard, and _save_pipeline assigns both fields by raw mutation (`graph.sources = ...; graph.active_source = ...`) with no re-validation. The invariant exists in the system but is encoded on the wrong (peripheral) type, leaving the source-of-truth type able to hold a selection that points at a non-existent source.
findings.recommended_design: Lift the `active_source in sources` check onto PipelineGraph as a `@model_validator(mode="after")` (the SidecarModel one can then delegate or be deduplicated). Pair with `validate_assignment=True` (see encapsulation finding) so the `_save_pipeline` raw assignments are re-checked. Consider modelling `sources` as a value object guaranteeing `"live"` is always present and first, since multiple call sites special-case that (routes/_helpers.py:689-696).
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: An out-of-range active_source silently routes execution/codegen down a non-existent branch; encoding it on the canonical type closes the gap the sidecar guard only half-covers.

findings.severity: high
findings.title: Graph models are mutable with no validate_assignment; in-place mutation silently desynchronises PipelineGraph's cached node_map/parents_of/fingerprint
findings.description: None of NodeData, GraphNode, GraphEdge, or PipelineGraph set `frozen=True` or `validate_assignment=True` (the only model_config anywhere is `ignored_types=(cached_property,)` on PipelineGraph, line 645). PipelineGraph went to real trouble to invalidate `node_map`/`parents_of`/`_haute_base_fingerprint` on the COPY path by overriding `model_copy` (lines 673-695) — but that protection is defeated by ANY in-place mutation: `graph.nodes.append(node)`, `graph.edges.pop()`, or `graph.nodes[0].id = "x"` mutates structure while the three @cached_property memos keep serving stale values (the cache is only cleared on copy, never on mutate). Because the fields are public and mutable, the carefully-built immutable-copy idiom is advisory, not enforced — a caller who mutates instead of `model_copy(update=...)` gets a silently incoherent graph (wrong parents, stale fingerprint -> wrong cache hits). `_save_pipeline.py:866-867` already mutates `graph.sources`/`active_source` in place, demonstrating the pattern is used in production code.
findings.recommended_design: Make the graph models immutable: `model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)` on GraphNode/NodeData/GraphEdge and add `frozen=True` to PipelineGraph (it already overrides model_copy as the evolution path, so frozen is the natural completion). If full immutability is too invasive for current callers, minimally set `validate_assignment=True` AND change the cached_property memos to be derived only through the copy path (or expose `nodes`/`edges` as read-only tuples). Convert the remaining in-place mutators (e.g. _save_pipeline source assignment) to `model_copy(update=...)`. This makes 'mutate without cache invalidation' unrepresentable.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Stale node_map/parents_of/fingerprint produce wrong wiring and wrong cache hits with no error — exactly the silent-wrongness class the model_copy override was written to prevent, left open on the mutation path.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:593-608 (NodeData.config) and the per-type *Config TypedDicts at 84-405
findings.severity: medium
findings.title: NodeData has an untyped `config: dict[str, Any]` even though a full discriminated union (nodeType -> per-type Config TypedDict) is defined in the same module
findings.description: _types.py defines ~20 precise TypedDicts (ApiInputConfig, ModelScoreConfig, RatingStepConfig, OptimiserConfig, ...) AND a NodeType StrEnum, yet NodeData stores `config: dict[str, Any]` with zero linkage to nodeType. The relationship 'nodeType=MODEL_SCORE => config conforms to ModelScoreConfig' exists only as prose docstrings and is re-checked ad hoc at runtime via `config.get(...)` everywhere (_builders.py:88-89, 466-467, 514-518; projection, codegen). Consequences: (a) wrong-shaped config for a node type is fully representable and only fails deep in a builder, often as a KeyError/None on a `.get` default rather than at the graph boundary; (b) the *_CONFIG_KEYS tuples (lines 149-160, 487-570) are a hand-maintained second source of truth for the same key sets, which can (and the codebase notes elsewhere they do) drift from the TypedDicts. The discriminated union that would make illegal nodeType/config pairings unrepresentable is 90% written but never wired into NodeData.
findings.recommended_design: Model NodeData as a discriminated union keyed on nodeType, e.g. a `Annotated[Union[ApiInputNodeData, ModelScoreNodeData, ...], Field(discriminator="nodeType")]` where each variant pins its concrete config (the TypedDicts become Pydantic models or `config: ModelScoreConfig`). Where full migration is too large, at minimum add a `@model_validator` on NodeData that validates `config` against the TypedDict selected by `nodeType` (TypedDicts are runtime-introspectable), and derive the *_CONFIG_KEYS tuples from the TypedDict `__annotations__` so the two representations cannot diverge.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Collapses 'config doesn't match node type' from a deep latent failure into a boundary-time type error and eliminates the duplicated CONFIG_KEYS drift surface; medium because most shapes are caught eventually by builders.

findings.severity: medium
findings.title: Contract permits inputs_by_parent to be set while inputs/outputs are None — an explicitly 'malformed' combination handled only at runtime
findings.description: Contract is `(inputs: frozenset|None, outputs: frozenset|None, inputs_by_parent: Mapping|None)`. Nothing in the dataclass or `from_user_declared` prevents `Contract(inputs=None, outputs=None, inputs_by_parent={'p': {...}})`. projection.py:1414-1417 documents this exact state as a 'malformed fan-in declaration' (a node declaring per-parent ownership without the concrete inputs/outputs needed to apportion it) and handles it defensively at projection time. So a known-invalid contract shape is constructible and is policed by scattered runtime logic rather than the type. Additionally `from_user_declared` is a 6-branch normaliser accepting Contract | dict | str-'opaque' | 2-tuple | duck-typed object | None (lines 63-108) — flexible at the edge, but it means the only guarantee that a Contract is internally consistent is whatever each branch happens to assert.
findings.recommended_design: Encode the dependency: add `__post_init__` (frozen dataclasses support it via object.__setattr__-free validation) raising when `inputs_by_parent is not None and (inputs is None or outputs is None)`. Better, model the two legitimate shapes as distinct types — e.g. `OpaqueContract` (no fields) vs `ConcreteContract(inputs: frozenset, outputs: frozenset, inputs_by_parent: Mapping[...] = {})` — and make `Contract = OpaqueContract | ConcreteContract`. Then 'per-parent ownership without concrete sides' is unrepresentable and projection.py's malformed-fan-in branch becomes dead code that can be deleted.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Removes one inconsistent-contract class and lets a runtime guard be deleted; medium because the malformed state mostly originates from user declarations already partially validated.

findings.location: src/haute/_contracts.py:20-32 (ColumnContract tuple alias) coexisting with Contract dataclass:35; conversions at 49-60
findings.severity: low
findings.title: Two parallel representations of a column contract (anonymous (set|None, set|None) tuple vs Contract dataclass) with lossy round-trips and reversed field order
findings.description: The same concept is modelled twice: `ColumnContract = tuple[set[str]|None, set[str]|None]` (produced, referenced) and the `Contract` dataclass (inputs, outputs, inputs_by_parent). They use OPPOSITE field order — the tuple is (produced/outputs, referenced/inputs) while Contract is (inputs, outputs) — and `from_tuple`/`to_tuple` (lines 49-60) hand-swap them, a classic site for silent transposition bugs. The tuple form also cannot carry `inputs_by_parent`, so `to_tuple()` is lossy and every `projection_contract(node).to_tuple()` call site (projection.py:1286, 1376, 1625, 2281) drops fan-in ownership. The registry stores `column_contract: Callable[..., Any]` (registry.py:65) returning the bare tuple, forcing the lift at every read.
findings.recommended_design: Make Contract the single representation and retire the public ColumnContract tuple to an internal codec only (or delete it). Have the registry's contract function return `Contract` directly. If a positional form must remain for back-compat, give it a NamedTuple with explicit `produced`/`referenced` fields so the order is self-documenting and the transpose risk disappears. Remove `to_tuple()` from hot projection paths so fan-in ownership is never silently dropped.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Low direct bug surface but removes a transpose-prone dual representation and a lossy conversion used in the projection hot path.

findings.severity: low
findings.title: GraphNode carries a second, stringly-typed `type` field that is effectively always 'pipelineNode' and duplicates/obscures the real discriminant nodeType
findings.description: GraphNode has `type: str = "pipelineNode"` (the React Flow node-renderer key) sitting next to the semantically meaningful `data.nodeType: NodeType`. The `type` field is an unconstrained `str` with a constant default; a grep of src shows it is never read for dispatch (no `node.type ==` comparisons in the backend) — all logic dispatches on `data.nodeType`. So the field is dead-weight from the backend's perspective yet fully mutable/arbitrary: `GraphNode(id=..., type="anything")` validates. This invites confusion ('which type field do I switch on?') and lets a wrong renderer key be persisted with no check.
findings.recommended_design: If the React Flow wrapper key must round-trip, constrain it: `type: Literal["pipelineNode"] = "pipelineNode"` (or a small Literal-union if other renderer keys are legitimate) so arbitrary strings are rejected and intent is explicit. Document that `data.nodeType` is the sole semantic discriminant. If the backend never needs `type`, consider dropping it from the canonical model and re-deriving it at the serialization boundary.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Low — primarily clarity and a tiny stringly-typed surface; the field is currently inert in the backend but is an attractive nuisance and an unvalidated persisted value.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:602-605 (GraphNode.id) — and pervasive `str` node-id parameters across _graph_utils.py, _topo.py, _contracts.py
findings.severity: low
findings.title: Node ids are bare `str` throughout, interchangeable with labels, ports, source names and func-names with no type distinction
findings.description: GraphNode.id is `str`, and every helper threads ids as `str`: build_parents_of, upstream_node_ids, ancestors/topo_sort_ids, Contract.inputs_by_parent keys, node_map keys, edge.source/target. In this module's vocabulary there are at least five distinct string roles — node id, sanitized func-name, port/handle name, source name ("live"/...), and human label — and they are all the same type, so passing a label where an id is expected (or an unsanitized id where a func-name is expected) type-checks. _config_io.py:174 ('Translate GUI node ids in config to ids produced by parsing') and the func-name-vs-id round-trip notes in _codegen_builders.py:1072 show these conversions are real and error-prone. A NewType wall would catch the swaps statically.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `NodeId = NewType("NodeId", str)` (and optionally `PortName`, `SourceName`, `FuncName`) and thread them through GraphNode.id, GraphEdge.source/target/handles, node_map, parents_of, Contract.inputs_by_parent keys, and the topo/ancestors helpers. NewType is zero-runtime-cost and would make 'passed a label/port where an id belongs' a type error. Adopt incrementally starting at the PipelineGraph public surface.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Low/medium: no runtime change and large mechanical scope, but it statically eliminates a recurring id/label/port/func-name confusion that several existing comments and the duplicate-func-name bug all touch.

findings.severity: low
findings.title: position modelled as open dict[str, float] permitting missing/extra keys; readers defensively `.get('x')` and tolerate None
findings.description: `position: dict[str, float]` with a default factory of `{"x": 0.0, "y": 0.0}` does not require the x/y keys nor forbid extras. routes/_helpers.py:788-789 reads it as `position.get("x")`/`position.get("y")` — i.e. the consumer assumes the keys may be absent and accepts `None`. So `GraphNode(id=..., position={})` or `{"x": 1.0}` or `{"x":1,"y":2,"z":3}` are all representable, and a half-populated position flows to downstream code as `(None, y)`. The invariant 'a position is exactly an (x, y) pair of floats' is structurally unenforced.
findings.recommended_design: Replace the open dict with a closed model: `class Position(BaseModel): x: float = 0.0; y: float = 0.0` (extras forbidden via `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")`), and type `position: Position`. This makes both fields always-present floats, eliminates the `.get(...)/None` defensive reads, and rejects stray keys at the boundary.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Low — UI metadata, not pricing-critical, but trivially fixable and removes a None-leak into layout code.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:654 (PipelineGraph.submodels) and the `graph.submodels or {}` pattern at codegen.py:904, routes/submodel.py:155, _graph_shape.py:93, _save_pipeline.py:671
findings.severity: low
findings.title: submodels is `dict[str, Any] | None` where None and {} are semantically identical, and its value type is fully untyped
findings.description: `submodels: dict[str, Any] | None = None` makes 'no submodels' representable two ways (None and {}), and indeed every reader normalises with `graph.submodels or {}` (codegen.py:904; routes/submodel.py:155; _graph_shape.py:93; _save_pipeline.py:671) — a tell that the Optional buys nothing but a recurring defensive idiom and a latent `None.items()`/`None[...]` hazard if a caller forgets it (routes/submodel.py:164 indexes `submodels[sm_name]` after the `or {}`). The value type `Any` also means the submodel metadata shape (file/childNodeIds/inputPorts/outputPorts — already captured by SubmodelConfig at line 584) is unenforced.
findings.recommended_design: Drop the Optional: `submodels: dict[str, SubmodelMeta] = Field(default_factory=dict)` so 'none' has one representation and readers can delete the `or {}` guard. Promote the value type from `Any` to a concrete model (turn the existing SubmodelConfig TypedDict into a Pydantic model `SubmodelMeta`). This removes the None/{} ambiguity and types the metadata that codegen and submodel routes depend on.
findings.recommended_severity_rationale: Low — mostly ergonomic and a small None-deref hazard; collapsing the dual empty-representation and typing the value is a clean, low-risk tightening.

results.coverage_note: Read in full: src/haute/_types.py, src/haute/graph_utils.py (re-export facade), src/haute/_graph_utils.py, src/haute/_contracts.py; plus supporting context src/haute/_topo.py, src/haute/_registry.py, and the relevant slices of projection.py/codegen.py/_builders.py/routes/_helpers.py to ground each finding in real call sites. Cross-checked against existing review corpus (review/02-findings/findings.json, review/04-exhaustive/raw/core.json + VERIFIED-BUGS.md, review/05-dimensions/raw/*) which is overwhelmingly behavioral/performance — no prior finding addresses the TYPE-INVARIANT design of these core types; the one adjacent item (duplicate-func-name-node-collapse) is a parser-layer behavioral bug and is explicitly distinguished from finding 1 (the type-level uniqueness invariant). ALREADY WELL-DESIGNED (called out, not re-reported): (1) NodeType as StrEnum with the DECORATOR<->NodeType bidirectional maps — clean, serialization-correct, single source of truth. (2) GraphEdge._reject_empty_handle validator (_types.py:620-635) — exemplary: refuses to coerce '' to None and documents why, making 'empty-string handle' unrepresentable. (3) PipelineGraph.model_copy override (673-695) invalidating cached_property memos — correct handling of the Pydantic shallow-copy footgun (the gap is only that in-place mutation bypasses it; see encapsulation finding). (4) _contracts.OPAQUE_CONTRACT sentinel registered explicitly to distinguish 'declared opaque' from 'forgot to declare' (lines 23-32) — a deliberate, well-reasoned design choice. (5) _contracts._freeze / _freeze_mapping coercion with strict non-string and empty-key rejection — good input hardening. (6) NodeRegistryEntry + validate_registry_complete (_registry.py) — turns exec/codegen drift into an import-time failure; strong example of promoting a drift invariant to a startup guarantee. Confidence on the two NewType-scale items (node-id primitive obsession, discriminated-union NodeData.config) is bounded by migration scope, not by doubt about the diagnosis — both are zero/low runtime-risk and adoptable incrementally from the PipelineGraph public surface.

findings.severity: high — removes the single largest bug-surface class in this subsystem: every node type can carry any other type's keys, and every consumer must defensively re-validate shape at the point of use
findings.title: NodeData.config is dict[str, Any] with no discriminated union tying nodeType to its config shape — the 18 per-type TypedDicts are documentation-only and never the actual field type
findings.description: NodeData declares `nodeType: NodeType` and `config: dict[str, Any]` as two independent fields. The pairing (apiInput→ApiInputConfig, ratingStep→RatingStepConfig, …) is the central invariant of the whole graph model, yet it exists only as a runtime convention: `_TYPED_DICT_BY_NODE_TYPE` in _config_validation.py maps the two for a *warn-only* key check (warn_unrecognized_config_keys never raises) and a *runtime* write-allowlist (_prepare_config_for_sidecar logs and drops off-spec keys). Nothing at the type level prevents constructing `NodeData(nodeType=NodeType.RATING_STEP, config={'baseInput': 'x', 'how': 'cross'})` — an edgeJoin config attached to a ratingStep node. Every consumer in the surface compensates with `config.get(...)` + isinstance ladders (e.g. _rating_step_config._validate_factors re-checks `isinstance(factors, list)` and re-checks each element is a str; _edge_join._required_role re-checks `isinstance(value, str)`; _banding_config repeatedly re-checks `isinstance(factor, dict)`). Because the TypedDicts are never used as the declared type, mypy verifies none of the ~200 `config.get('key')` call sites against the per-type schema, so a typo'd key, a key read on the wrong node type, or a shape drift between writer and reader is invisible statically and only surfaces (if at all) as a runtime KeyError/ValueError or a silent default.
findings.recommended_design: Promote the existing TypedDicts into a Pydantic discriminated union and make it the type of the config field. Either (a) give each per-type config a Pydantic model with `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` and a literal `node_type` tag, then `NodeConfig = Annotated[ApiInputConfig | DataSourceConfig | …, Field(discriminator='node_type')]` and replace NodeData with a tagged union of `(NodeType, NodeConfig)` pairs; or (b) keep NodeData but type config as the union and add a `@model_validator(mode='after')` that asserts `type(self.config) is _MODEL_BY_NODE_TYPE[self.nodeType]`. Pydantic then rejects cross-type configs and unknown keys at construction/deserialisation (the wire boundary), `_prepare_config_for_sidecar`'s drop-allowlist and `warn_unrecognized_config_keys` collapse into the parse step, and every `config.get(...)` becomes attribute access type-checked against the correct schema. This makes 'wrong key on wrong node type' unrepresentable rather than warn-logged.
findings.recommended_design_note: Well-designed already: NodeType (StrEnum, single source of truth shared with frontend) and the GraphEdge handle validator (rejects '' rather than coercing to None) are exemplary — the fix is to extend that same rigor from the edges to the node config payload.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:111 DataSourceConfig.sourceType / :166 ModelScoreConfig.sourceType / :386 OptimiserApplyConfig.sourceType; compared as bare string literals in ~15 files (deploy/_bundler.py:75,89; deploy/_scorer.py:170,172,531; execution.py:158,448,542; _builders.py:544; routes/pipeline.py:138; cli/_helpers.py:230; etc.)
findings.severity: high — a single mistyped literal ('registerd', 'flatfile') silently routes to the wrong loader/else-branch with no error; an enum makes every such typo a compile-time failure across all ~15 comparison sites
findings.title: sourceType is a free `str` with three incompatible per-node-type domains, hand-compared against bare string literals in 15+ files instead of an enum
findings.description: Three different node types each have a `sourceType: str` field whose legal values are documented only in trailing comments and differ per type: dataSource = {flat_file, databricks}; modelScore = {run, registered}; optimiserApply = {file, run, registered}. The value is built stringly (_config_builder.py:97 hardcodes `config['sourceType']='databricks'`, :104 `'flat_file'`) and consumed by ~15 sites that compare against bare literals (`== 'databricks'`, `== 'run'`, `== 'registered'`, `== 'file'`). There is no enum, no Literal union enforced at the type level, and no exhaustiveness: every consumer is an `if ==…: … elif ==…: … else:` ladder where the `else` silently means 'treat as flat_file' / 'don't load MLflow'. A typo'd literal in any one site, or a new sourceType added without updating a branch, produces silent mis-routing (e.g. a 'registered' model treated as live 'run'), which is exactly the class behind existing behavioral finding #65-family deploy/validate divergences. The frontend already hardcodes the matching literals in DataSourceEditor/ModelScoreEditor/OptimiserApplyEditor JS, so the contract is duplicated across the language boundary with no shared source of truth.
findings.recommended_design: Define per-type StrEnums next to NodeType (e.g. `class DataSourceKind(StrEnum): FLAT_FILE='flat_file'; DATABRICKS='databricks'`, `class ModelSource(StrEnum): RUN='run'; REGISTERED='registered'`, `class OptimiserApplySource(StrEnum): FILE='file'; RUN='run'; REGISTERED='registered'`) — mirroring the existing SourceFormat/ExecutionProfile StrEnums already in the codebase. Type the TypedDict/Pydantic field as the enum (StrEnum still serialises to the same JSON string, so the wire format is unchanged and the frontend literals keep working). Then `match source: case ModelSource.RUN: … case ModelSource.REGISTERED: …` gives mypy exhaustiveness; an unhandled/new variant is a type error, and a typo'd literal is rejected at deserialisation. Validation moves once, to the boundary, instead of being re-encoded as ad-hoc string equality in every branch.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:227 RatingStepConfig.operation / :219 RatingTable.onMissing; validated by frozenset membership at src/haute/_rating.py:290-291,403-415,475-483
findings.severity: medium-high — converts three scattered runtime frozenset re-validations (_SUPPORTED_COMBINE_OPERATIONS, _SUPPORTED_ON_MISSING) into one type-level guarantee, and removes the `str(operation or 'multiply')` silent-default trap
findings.title: Rating `operation`/`onMissing` are `str` re-validated against module-private frozensets at materialisation time, not enums — the legal domain lives in three places and the value is silently coerced
findings.description: RatingStepConfig.operation and RatingTable.onMissing are declared `str` (legal values only in comments: operation = multiply|add|min|max, onMissing = error|neutral). The actual domain is enforced at runtime by _rating.py via `_SUPPORTED_COMBINE_OPERATIONS = frozenset({'multiply','add','min','max'})` and `_SUPPORTED_ON_MISSING = frozenset({'error','neutral'})`, checked in `_normalise_combine_operation` (line 475) and `_normalise_on_missing` (line 403). These two frozensets are the real source of truth, but they are private to _rating.py and invisible to the TypedDict, the config builder (_config_builder.py:165-179 builds `operation`/`combinedOutputs` with no validation and `str(op)`), and the sidecar codec. The combine path additionally does `str(operation or 'multiply')` — an empty/falsy operation is silently coerced to 'multiply' rather than rejected, so a config that lost its operation key prices as a product silently. Because the field is `str`, the builder, the codec, and the executor cannot agree statically that only four operations exist; a fifth operation added to the engine without touching _config_builder, or a misspelled 'mutiply' in a hand-edited sidecar, is caught (if at all) only deep inside `_combine_rating_columns` at materialisation, far from where the config was constructed.
findings.recommended_design: Replace with StrEnums owned by the type module: `class RatingOperation(StrEnum): MULTIPLY='multiply'; ADD='add'; MIN='min'; MAX='max'` and `class RatingMissPolicy(StrEnum): ERROR='error'; NEUTRAL='neutral'`. Type operation/onMissing/combinedOutputs[].operation as these enums; delete the private frozensets in _rating.py and switch `_combine_rating_columns` to `match RatingOperation(operation)` for compiler-checked exhaustiveness (the neutral-element table becomes a total mapping keyed by the enum). Keep an explicit required default at the model layer (`operation: RatingOperation = RatingOperation.MULTIPLY`) instead of the `or 'multiply'` coercion, so a present-but-empty value is a validation error rather than a silent product.

findings.location: src/haute/_edge_join.py:28 (_ALLOWED_HOW), :159-187 (build_edge_join_kwargs); type declared at src/haute/_types.py:139 EdgeJoinConfig.how
findings.severity: medium — promotes the join-strategy domain to an enum and (more importantly) makes the on-XOR-(leftOn,rightOn) key invariant representable so the 'both set' / 'cross with keys' illegal states can be eliminated at the type boundary
findings.title: edgeJoin `how` is a `str` re-validated against a private frozenset, and the mutually-exclusive on / (leftOn,rightOn) key invariant is enforced only by imperative ConfigError ladders, not by the type
findings.description: EdgeJoinConfig.how is `str`; the real domain is `_ALLOWED_HOW = frozenset({'inner','left','right','full','semi','anti','cross'})`, a module-private constant in _edge_join.py re-checked in build_edge_join_kwargs (line 160). Separately, the join-key shape encodes a non-trivial invariant entirely in runtime guards (lines 171-187): a cross join MUST have no keys; a non-cross join must have EITHER `on` OR both `leftOn`+`rightOn` but never both; and leftOn/rightOn must have equal length. The TypedDict declares all four keys as independent optional `str | list[str]` fields, so `EdgeJoinConfig(how='cross', on='id')` and `EdgeJoinConfig(how='inner', on='id', leftOn='a')` are both representable illegal states that only fail when build_edge_join_kwargs runs. This is the exact class behind existing behavioral finding 04-#381 (frontend writes unequal-length leftOn/rightOn → backend ConfigError at execute). The how-domain is also duplicated stringly across the frontend (edgeJoinValidation.ts) and the runtime narrowing helper hardcodes the mechanically-narrowable subset as another literal set `{'inner','left','semi','anti'}` at line 268.
findings.recommended_design: (1) `class JoinHow(StrEnum): INNER; LEFT; RIGHT; FULL; SEMI; ANTI; CROSS` and type `how` as JoinHow; delete _ALLOWED_HOW and the line-160 recheck; switch narrow_join_parent_demand's `{'inner','left','semi','anti'}` to a JoinHow membership set. (2) Make the key invariant unrepresentable by modelling the keys as a discriminated union instead of four loose optionals: `CrossJoin(how: Literal[CROSS])` (no key fields), `OnJoin(on: JoinKey)`, `LeftRightJoin(left_on: JoinKey, right_on: JoinKey)` where JoinKey is a NewType/validated list guaranteeing ≥1 non-empty string and a Pydantic validator enforces `len(left_on)==len(right_on)`. build_edge_join_kwargs then `match`es on the variant and can no longer receive an over- or under-specified key set — the three ConfigError branches at 171-187 become structurally impossible.
findings.recommended_design_note: Well-designed already in this file: JoinKey = str | list[str] as an alias, and resolve_edge_join_role_indices's exhaustive base/join distinctness + connectivity checks are good defensive runtime validation — the gap is that none of it is reflected in the static config type.

findings.severity: medium — closes a documented-vs-actual domain mismatch (TypedDict comment lists values that do not exist) and removes the silent `or 'continuous'` coercion that lets an unknown banding type masquerade as continuous until late
findings.title: BandingFactor.banding is `str` whose documented domain ('continuous'|'discrete') contradicts the engine's real domain ('categorical'|'breakpoints'|'continuous'); the value is silently coerced and the rules shape depends on it untyped
findings.description: BandingFactor.banding is declared `str` with the comment `# "continuous" | "discrete"` (_types.py:189). That comment is wrong: the engine never recognises 'discrete'; _banding_config branches only on 'categorical' and 'breakpoints' (_expand_rule_map lines 36/44, _compact_rule_map lines 105/115) with 'continuous' as the implicit fall-through, and the compaction gate is `_COMPACT_RULE_TYPES = frozenset({'categorical','breakpoints'})` (line 9). So the authoritative domain is {categorical, breakpoints, continuous}, encoded as scattered literals and a private frozenset, and the documentation advertises a value ('discrete') that is silently treated as continuous. _banding_type (line 12) does `str(factor.get('banding') or 'continuous')`, so a missing OR unrecognised-falsy value is coerced to 'continuous' rather than rejected — an illegal banding type only fails much later (and only for non-continuous-shaped rules) via the generic `f"{banding_type} banding rules must be a list"` ValueError. Compounding this, BandingFactor.rules is typed `list[dict[str, Any]]` even though the field legitimately holds a dict-map in the sidecar form (expand_rule_map consumes `dict[Any, Any]`), so the declared type does not even describe the on-disk shape and the discriminator that decides which shape applies (banding) is itself untyped.
findings.recommended_design: `class BandingKind(StrEnum): CONTINUOUS='continuous'; CATEGORICAL='categorical'; BREAKPOINTS='breakpoints'` and type `banding: BandingKind = BandingKind.CONTINUOUS`. Then make BandingFactor a discriminated union on BandingKind so each variant carries its correct rules shape: ContinuousFactor (rules absent), CategoricalFactor(rules: list[{value,assignment}] | dict[str,scalar]), BreakpointFactor(rules: list[{boundary,label}] | dict[str,scalar]). Replace the `or 'continuous'` coercion with enum validation so an unknown banding type is rejected at parse time; delete _COMPACT_RULE_TYPES (membership becomes `kind in {BandingKind.CATEGORICAL, BandingKind.BREAKPOINTS}`) and fix the docstring. This makes 'discrete' (and any other typo) unrepresentable and ties the rules-shape branch to a typed discriminator.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:202-205 RatingTableEntry (empty body) & :220 RatingTable.entries: list[dict[str, Any]]; consumed at src/haute/_rating_step_config.py:148-204 (_normalise_entry_rows/_compact_entry_rows) and :207-258 (_expand_entries_map)
findings.severity: medium — the entry type is a no-op placeholder so every invariant (factor keys present, single scalar value, value/outputColumn agreement, dual list-or-map shape) is enforced only by hand-rolled runtime walks; making the row shape a real type removes a recurring source of write/read asymmetry bugs
findings.title: RatingTableEntry is an empty TypedDict and RatingTable.entries is list[dict[str,Any]], so the canonical-row invariant (exactly the table's factor keys + one scalar `value`) is entirely runtime-asserted and the compact-map alternative shape is untyped
findings.description: RatingTableEntry (_types.py:202-205) has an empty body with only a comment ('Keys are dynamic factor names'), so it contributes nothing — it is `dict` with documentation. RatingTable.entries is `list[dict[str, Any]]`, but the field is bimodal: on disk it is a nested factor→value MAP (compact sidecar), and in memory it is a row-ARRAY (`{factor: key, …, 'value': scalar}`). The whole of _rating_step_config.py exists to convert and re-validate between these untyped shapes: _entry_value re-derives the single value and rejects the 'both value and outputColumn disagree' illegal state (line 129-138); _normalise_entry_rows re-asserts every factor key is present and non-null (line 161-163); _validate_rating_value re-checks scalar-ness/finiteness/non-bool at line 82-101; _expand_entries_map re-walks depth to match factor count. None of these invariants are expressible because the row type is `dict[str, Any]`. This is precisely the surface where the existing behavioral findings cluster (04-#63/#68 write/read key-normalisation asymmetry, 05 float-key divergence): an untyped dual-shape dict is the substrate that makes those asymmetries possible, because there is no single typed definition of 'a canonical rating row' that both the writer and reader must satisfy.
findings.recommended_design: Model the two shapes explicitly. (1) Canonical in-memory row: a Pydantic model `RatingRow` with the factor columns and a single `value: float` (or a NewType `RatingValue` carrying the finite-non-bool invariant validated once), replacing list[dict[str,Any]]. (2) The compact sidecar map as its own recursive type `CompactEntries = dict[str, 'CompactEntries | RatingValue]` so the nesting-depth-equals-factor-count invariant is at least shape-checkable. Then expand/compact become typed total functions `CompactEntries -> list[RatingRow]` and the value/outputColumn agreement + factor-presence checks move into RatingRow's validator (one place, runtime-once at the boundary) instead of being re-litigated in _entry_value/_normalise_entry_rows/_expand_entries_map. Delete the empty RatingTableEntry. This gives the writer and reader a shared typed contract, which is the structural fix for the write/read asymmetry class.
findings.recommended_design_note: Well-designed already: the canonical-key helper normalise_rating_key being shared by engine + sidecar + trace is the right single-source-of-truth instinct; the gap is that the row/table that holds those keys is not itself typed.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:268-275 ExternalFileConfig (fileType, modelClass) & :177 ModelScoreConfig.task / :296-298 ModellingConfig.algorithm/task; builder at src/haute/_config_builder.py:213-218
findings.severity: medium — these are closed enumerations dispatched on at load/score/train time; an enum removes the silent-default branches (e.g. fileType default 'pickle', modelClass default 'classifier') and gives exhaustive dispatch
findings.title: Loader/model discriminators (fileType, modelClass, task, algorithm) are free `str` with comment-only domains and string-defaulted construction, dispatched via untyped branches
findings.description: Several closed-set discriminators are typed `str`: ExternalFileConfig.fileType (comment: pickle|json|joblib|catboost), ExternalFileConfig.modelClass (classifier|regressor, catboost-only), ModelScoreConfig.task & ModellingConfig.task (regression|classification), ModellingConfig.algorithm (catboost|glm). _config_builder.py:213-218 constructs these stringly with silent defaults (`fileType = decorator_kwargs.get('file_type', 'pickle')`; only sets modelClass `if config['fileType']=='catboost'`), so a fileType typo silently means 'pickle' and a non-catboost fileType simply omits modelClass with no signal. modelClass is moreover a conditional field — it is only meaningful when fileType=='catboost' — which is an illegal-state-by-construction (modelClass can be present with fileType='json', or absent with fileType='catboost') that the flat TypedDict cannot express. task/algorithm drive runtime dispatch in the scorer/trainer via the same `== 'classification'` / `== 'catboost'` literal style seen elsewhere. None of these has an enum despite the codebase already using StrEnum freely (SourceFormat, ExecutionProfile, ChunkCapabilityKind).
findings.recommended_design: Introduce StrEnums: `FileType{PICKLE,JSON,JOBLIB,CATBOOST}`, `CatboostModelClass{CLASSIFIER,REGRESSOR}`, `MLTask{REGRESSION,CLASSIFICATION}`, `Algorithm{CATBOOST,GLM}`, and type the fields accordingly. For the conditional modelClass, make ExternalFileConfig a discriminated union on FileType where only the CatboostFile variant carries `model_class: CatboostModelClass` (required there, absent elsewhere) — eliminating the 'modelClass present iff catboost' invariant as a runtime concern. Replace the string-defaulted builder construction with enum defaults validated at the boundary so a typo is rejected rather than coerced to pickle/classifier. Dispatch sites switch to `match` for exhaustiveness.

findings.location: src/haute/_config_io.py:323-356 collect_node_configs / :359-378 config_load_errors / :167-193 _remap_config_ids_for_saved_graph; marker key '_load_error' and 'instanceOf' read via config.get on dict[str,Any]
findings.severity: low-medium — in-band magic-string markers stuffed into the same untyped dict as real config are easy to typo and impossible to distinguish from data; lifting them to typed fields removes a silent-skip failure mode in the save path
findings.title: Control-flow markers ('_load_error', 'instanceOf') are smuggled as magic string keys inside the untyped config dict rather than typed fields on NodeData
findings.description: The save/collect path keys behaviour off magic strings stored inside config: collect_node_configs skips a node when `config.get('instanceOf')` is truthy (line 342) or `config.get('_load_error')` is set (line 344); config_load_errors keys off the same `_load_error` marker (line 369). These are not user config — they are out-of-band control state (an instance pointer; a load-failure sentinel injected when a sidecar fails to parse) — yet they live in the same `dict[str, Any]` as `path`/`tables`/etc., distinguished only by an underscore-prefix convention that _strip_internal_keys (line 64) and the `not k.startswith('_')` filters elsewhere must constantly special-case. A typo'd marker ('_loadError', 'instance_of') silently changes save behaviour (a failed-load node could be overwritten/lost, or an instance node could be re-serialised). Because the markers are string keys on an Any dict, mypy cannot verify any of these read/write sites, and the underscore-prefix overload (frontend `_status`/`_columns` ephemeral UI state ALSO uses underscore keys) conflates 'frontend ephemeral' with 'backend load-error sentinel' in one namespace.
findings.recommended_design: Lift the control markers out of config into typed fields on NodeData: `instance_of: str | None = None` and `load_error: str | None = None` (or a small `NodeStatus` model). collect_node_configs/config_load_errors then branch on `node.data.load_error is not None` and `node.data.instance_of` — type-checked, un-typoable, and cleanly separated from the user-authored config payload. If the markers must stay on the wire dict for frontend-compat reasons, at minimum define module-level Final constants for the key names and a typed accessor, so the magic strings have a single definition and the read sites are greppable/checkable.
findings.recommended_design_note: Well-designed already: the path-traversal guards in config_path_for_node/load_node_config (reject '..'/separators, assert is_relative_to config root) and the duplicate-key rejection in _load_json_object are strong boundary invariants worth preserving as-is.
