findings.location: src/haute/_registry.py:47-65 (NodeRegistryEntry); cross-cut with src/haute/_builders.py:464-1295 (every @_register'd _build_*) and src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:337-1117 (every _gen_*/template)
findings.severity: high — this is the type-level root cause of the entire codegen<->executor equivalence cluster (catalog items 1,2,3): nothing in the registry encodes whether a NodeType is a pure passthrough or applies stateful logic, so the exec builder and the codegen builder independently (re)decide and silently disagree.
findings.title: Passthrough-vs-stateful-apply is unencoded in NodeRegistryEntry; the two sides can disagree by construction
findings.description: NodeRegistryEntry bundles `exec` and `codegen` as two free function pointers with NO shared declaration of the node's execution semantics. For banding/ratingStep/modelScore the exec builder applies a real operation AND the codegen template emits a call to the SAME `apply_*_from_config`/`score_from_config` helper — they agree only because two humans kept two code paths in sync. For optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander the exec builder applies an operation (e.g. _build_optimiser_apply -> optimiser_apply_fn loads the artifact and adds __optimiser_version__) while the codegen template emits `return {first}` (a pure passthrough). The registry type cannot tell these classes apart, so `validate_registry_complete` (which only checks both fields are non-None) reports the broken pair as healthy. The illegal state is: `entry.exec` is stateful but `entry.codegen` is passthrough (or vice-versa). It is representable, constructible, and currently constructed in production.
findings.recommended_design: Make the dispatch SEMANTICS a field, not an implication. Add a `kind: NodeSemantics` (StrEnum: PASSTHROUGH | STATEFUL | SOURCE) to NodeRegistryEntry and require it at registration (`register_exec(node_type, *, kind=...)`). For STATEFUL nodes, require an `apply: ApplyFn` helper on the entry that BOTH the exec builder and the codegen-emitted body call (see separate finding). Extend `validate_registry_complete` to assert: PASSTHROUGH entries' codegen emits only `return {first}` AND exec returns `_passthrough_fn`; STATEFUL entries carry a non-None `apply` and their codegen body references it. This converts 'codegen forgot to embed the apply call' from a silent pricing divergence into an import-time RuntimeError.

findings.location: src/haute/_registry.py:48-65 (NodeRegistryEntry has no `apply` slot); src/haute/_builders.py:824-834 (_build_rating_step calls _apply_rating_step_outputs) vs src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:360-369 (_RATING_STEP emits apply_rating_step_from_config); src/haute/_builders.py:999-1038 (optimiser_apply_fn -> _dispatch_apply) with NO codegen counterpart
findings.severity: high — promotes the 'one apply helper shared between executor and codegen' rule from an unwritten convention (kept by discipline for 3 node types, violated for 4) to a constructor-enforced invariant.
findings.title: The 'single shared apply helper per stateful node' invariant exists only by convention; it should be a required field on the entry
findings.description: The codebase already KNOWS the correct pattern: stateful nodes route through a single `apply_*_from_config`/`score_from_config` helper that the executor calls directly and the generated standalone file calls via its body. But this is enforced nowhere — it is replicated by hand in banding/ratingStep/modelScore and simply omitted for optimiser/optimiserApply/modelling/scenarioExpander, which is exactly the bug surface. Because there is no `apply` field on NodeRegistryEntry, the registry cannot require 'a STATEFUL node MUST share one apply callable across both sides', so the equivalence is a runtime property discovered only by executing the saved file (catalog items 2,3) rather than a type-level guarantee.
findings.recommended_design: Add `apply: ApplyFn | None = None` to NodeRegistryEntry, where `ApplyFn = Callable[[_Frame, Mapping[str, Any]], _Frame]` is the config-driven transform. Refactor each stateful exec builder to call `entry.apply(lf, config)` and each stateful codegen template to emit a body that imports and calls the SAME helper (the banding/ratingStep mechanism, generalised). Make `register_exec(..., kind=STATEFUL)` reject a missing `apply`. Then a single registration site is the source of truth for the operation, and the executor and codegen are wired to the identical callable BY CONSTRUCTION — they cannot drift because there is only one function. This is the concrete realisation of 'could the registry enforce by construction that every stateful node shares one apply helper between executor and codegen?': yes — make the helper a mandatory field and dispatch both sides through it.

findings.location: src/haute/_registry.py:60-65 (exec/codegen/column_contract are mutable public fields); set incrementally at src/haute/_registry.py:101-103,119,138
findings.severity: medium — the slots dataclass is mutable and public; any code holding an entry can null/overwrite exec, codegen, or column_contract after validation, defeating the completeness invariant that the module's docstring promises.
findings.title: NodeRegistryEntry fields are mutable-public, so the 'complete after validate' invariant is not preserved post-construction
findings.description: The module guarantees (docstring, validate_registry_complete) that after import every entry has both sides populated. But entries are `@dataclass(slots=True)` with plain public attributes and the `_entry()` helper hands out the live mutable object. `register_exec` guards against DUPLICATE assignment (raises on re-set), yet nothing prevents `NODE_REGISTRY[nt].codegen = None` or reassignment from arbitrary code after `_REGISTRY_READY` is set. The invariant is enforced once (at import) and then left unguarded — an 'optional-everywhere until validated, then assumed total' shape. get_exec/get_codegen/get_column_contract re-check for None on every call (the runtime tax of not having a total type), which is the symptom of the missing guarantee.
findings.recommended_design: After completion, freeze the registry into an immutable total mapping: build entries via a builder, then in `ensure_registry_ready` construct `NODE_REGISTRY_FINAL: Mapping[NodeType, FrozenNodeEntry]` where FrozenNodeEntry is `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` with NON-optional `exec: ExecFn`, `codegen: CodegenFn`, `column_contract: ColumnContractFn` (and the proposed `kind`/`apply`). get_exec/get_codegen then index a total map and never branch on None. This makes 'incomplete entry' unrepresentable after init and deletes the per-call None checks at _registry.py:148-163, _builders.py:372, codegen.py:461.

findings.location: src/haute/_builders.py:141 (NodeBuilder return tuple) and src/haute/_builders.py:1317,1367 (_build_node_fn returns the 3-tuple); registry alias src/haute/_registry.py:41 (ExecFn -> tuple[str, Callable, bool]); consumed at src/haute/_execute_lazy.py:416,1118 and src/haute/pipeline.py:33,113
findings.type_name: ExecFn / NodeBuilder return tuple[str, Callable[..., Any], bool]
findings.severity: medium — the source/transform classification of a node lives only as a bare positional bool recomputed inside each builder (e.g. _builders.py:1249 `is_source = not _src_names`), with no link to the per-NodeType semantics; this is the same 'semantics decided ad hoc per builder' pattern that produced the passthrough divergence, applied to the source axis.
findings.title: Builder result is an unnamed (str, Callable, bool) tuple; `is_source` is a positional boolean with no structural meaning
findings.description: Every exec builder returns `(func_name, fn, is_source)`. The third element is a raw bool whose meaning ('the executor may call this with zero inputs and must skip the no-input guard') is documented only in prose at _builders.py:1241-1250. Two failure modes follow from the primitive: (a) positional fragility — a builder that swaps the last two return values is a type error mypy cannot catch (both are truthy objects in a `tuple[str, Callable, bool]` only because the bool is last); (b) the `is_source` truth is derived inconsistently — POLARS computes it from `not _src_names` at build time, pipeline.py:113 derives it from `len(params)==0`, trace.py:792 derives it from `nid in source_ids` — three independent definitions of the same concept with no single typed owner.
findings.recommended_design: Replace the tuple with a frozen dataclass `BuiltNode(func_name: str, fn: Callable[..., _Frame], role: NodeRole)` where `NodeRole` is a StrEnum (SOURCE | TRANSFORM). Name the field so reorder bugs become type errors and so the source/transform axis is a single typed concept rather than three ad hoc booleans. If the source-ness is genuinely a per-NodeType property (it is for all types except POLARS' self-contained-code special case), hoist it onto the registry entry (`kind=SOURCE`) so it is declared once per type, and let only the POLARS builder override at build time.

findings.location: src/haute/_registry.py:60-61 (exec/codegen default None) and 65 (column_contract default None); enforced-required at runtime in src/haute/_registry.py:148-163 and src/haute/_builders.py:371-378 / src/haute/_contracts.py:158-165
findings.severity: medium — `column_contract: Callable | None` is declared optional but is in fact REQUIRED for every NodeType (get_column_contract raises KeyError if None), and `validate_registry_complete` does NOT check it (only exec/codegen). So a NodeType can pass import-time validation with a null contract and only blow up later during the projection pass.
findings.title: column_contract is type-Optional and excluded from completeness validation, yet treated as mandatory at use sites
findings.description: Three fields default to None to allow incremental registration, but they fall into two different invariant classes that the type conflates. exec/codegen are checked by validate_registry_complete. column_contract is NOT — yet get_column_contract / _contracts.py treat a None contract as a hard error ('Every builder in NODE_REGISTRY must also register a contract'). The result is a hidden required-invariant: the type says 'optional', the docstring says 'must', and the validation pass silently omits it. A future NodeType registered with `register_exec` but no `column_contract=`/`opaque=` would import cleanly and only fail when the checkpoint projection runs — exactly the class of late, hard-to-localise failure the registry was created to eliminate.
findings.recommended_design: Either (a) make column_contract non-optional in the frozen final entry (see the freeze finding) and add it to validate_registry_complete's missing-set check alongside exec/codegen, so a missing contract fails loudly at import like the others; or (b) if 'no contract' is a legitimate state, model it explicitly as `column_contract: ColumnContractFn` defaulting to a module-level OPAQUE_CONTRACT_FN rather than None, so the 'declared opaque' vs 'forgot to declare' distinction the docstring cares about is encoded as a real value, not None-overloading. Option (a) is preferred given the code already insists the contract is mandatory.

findings.location: src/haute/_types.py:25-50 (NodeType enum) with no semantic grouping; consequence visible at src/haute/_builders.py:1288-1295 (_build_submodel/_build_submodel_port passthrough) vs src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:1094-1117 (_gen_submodel raises)
findings.severity: low — the SUBMODEL/SUBMODEL_PORT pair are placeholders that are illegal to dispatch on at codegen time (the codegen builder is a 'should never be reached' raiser), but NodeType gives them equal standing with real executable types, so 'a placeholder node reached real dispatch' is representable rather than excluded at the type boundary.
findings.title: Placeholder NodeTypes (SUBMODEL/SUBMODEL_PORT) are indistinguishable in the type from executable NodeTypes
findings.description: SUBMODEL and SUBMODEL_PORT are boundary placeholders that flatten_graph/graph_to_code_multi must remove before dispatch; the codegen builders for them are pure tripwires that raise RuntimeError if ever invoked (_gen_submodel_placeholder_unreachable). This is a runtime-checked invariant ('these never reach codegen dispatch') standing in for what the type could express directly. Because NodeType is one flat StrEnum, every consumer that switches on NodeType (registry validation, builder dispatch, projection) must treat placeholders as if they were schedulable, and the 'unreachable' contract is re-asserted defensively in two builders plus prose rather than guaranteed structurally.
findings.recommended_design: Partition the closed set: keep NodeType as the wire enum, but introduce a derived `ExecutableNodeType` (e.g. a Literal-union or a `@property is_placeholder` plus a typed `executable_node_types: frozenset[NodeType]`) and have the dispatch surface (_build_node_fn / get_codegen) accept only executable types, with the placeholder filter applied once at the graph-flattening boundary that returns the narrowed type. Then 'codegen dispatched on a submodel placeholder' is caught by the type of the dispatch function's parameter rather than by a runtime raise inside the builder. This keeps the loud-failure intent while moving the guarantee up to the boundary where the narrowing actually happens.

results.coverage_note: Read in full: src/haute/_registry.py, src/haute/_codegen_builders.py, and the NodeType/config/GraphNode type definitions in src/haute/_types.py; src/haute/_builders.py read in full across two pages (1-1412, 1413-1734). Cross-checked existing findings to avoid duplication: review/02-findings/catalog.md items 1-3 and findings.json document the BEHAVIORAL symptom (semantic-equivalence: standalone-vs-canvas pricing divergence) and point the root cause at the codegen TEMPLATES (_codegen_builders.py) and pipeline.py's non-NODE_REGISTRY dispatch; review/02-findings/repro/codegen__passthrough-body-node-types-not-runtime-equivalent.py and codegen__optimiserapply-standalone-passthrough-no-apply.py are the repros. review/04-exhaustive contains no registry/type-system design entries. The six findings here are the NEW type-&-invariant-design angle on the SAME cluster: they target the registry/builder TYPES (NodeRegistryEntry, ExecFn return tuple, column_contract optionality, NodeType placeholder modeling) and propose making the passthrough/stateful and source/transform distinctions type-level, plus a mandatory shared `apply` field so executor and codegen route through one helper by construction. WELL-DESIGNED types observed (no action): the Contract dataclass (src/haute/_builders.py:161-271) with its exhaustive from_user_declared normalisation that fails loud on malformed input; GraphEdge._reject_empty_handle (src/haute/_types.py:620-635) which makes empty-string handles unrepresentable; PipelineGraph.model_copy cached-property invalidation (src/haute/_types.py:673-695) which makes stale-memo-after-copy unrepresentable; the SolveResultLike Protocol hierarchy (src/haute/_types.py:416-485); and the duplicate-registration guards in register_exec/register_codegen/set_codegen which already make double-registration unrepresentable. findings.location: src/haute/routes/_job_lifecycle.py:15-46, 91-96 (status constants + require_job_status) cross-referenced with src/haute/schemas.py:33-42 (JobStatus)
findings.severity: high — eliminates an entire class of silent status-vocabulary drift across 7 files; today a status added/renamed in one place but not the other is only caught (if at all) by a runtime ValueError after a job is already mis-stored
findings.title: Two independent, manually-synchronised job-status vocabularies bridged by a runtime cast
findings.description: `_job_lifecycle.py` imports the authoritative 8-member `JobStatus = Literal[...]` from schemas (line 13) and then immediately re-declares the SAME vocabulary as a parallel set of bare string constants (`RUNNING_STATUS = "running"`, `COMPLETED_STATUS = "completed"`, ... lines 15-22) plus a `TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS` map and a `JOB_STATUSES` frozenset (lines 34-45). These are two disconnected sources of truth for the same closed set of strings: nothing at type-check time forces `JOB_STATUSES` to equal the members of `JobStatus`, or `RUNNING_STATUS` to be a `JobStatus` member. The disconnect is then papered over at runtime: `require_job_status` (91-96) validates `status` against the `JOB_STATUSES` *frozenset* and then `cast(JobStatus, status)` — the cast asserts a relationship the compiler cannot verify. If `JobStatus` gains a member (e.g. a new terminal state) but `JOB_STATUSES`/the constants are not updated, `require_job_status` will *reject a legitimate status as corrupt*; if the reverse, a value outside `JobStatus` flows through the cast unchecked. mypy/pyright catch neither.
findings.recommended_design: Make `JobStatus` the single source of truth and derive everything else from it. Replace the bare constants with a `StrEnum` (`class JobStatus(StrEnum): RUNNING='running'; COMPLETED='completed'; ...`) defined once in schemas, or keep the Literal and derive `JOB_STATUSES = frozenset(get_args(JobStatus))` so the frozenset is provably the Literal's members. Similarly type `TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS: Mapping[TerminalReason, JobStatus]` and add a module-level assertion/test that `set(TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS.values()) | {RUNNING}` exactly equals the JobStatus members. With a StrEnum, `require_job_status` becomes `JobStatus(status)` (raises on unknown) with no `cast`, turning the runtime cast into a type-level guarantee.

findings.location: src/haute/routes/_job_store.py:80, 342, 360, 369, 382-388, 425-432, 458, 475, 534-541 (job record is dict[str, Any] throughout)
findings.type_name: JobStore job record (dict[str, Any]) — the implicit Job entity
findings.severity: high — the central state object of every long-running operation (train/optimise/explore) has zero structural typing; every field access is `.get("key")` returning Any, so misspelled keys, wrong-type values, and missing required fields (e.g. no `status`) are all constructible and only fail (if ever) deep downstream
findings.title: The job record — the engine's core async-result type — is an untyped dict[str, Any] with stringly-keyed required fields
findings.description: Every public JobStore method speaks `dict[str, Any]`: `create_job(initial_status: dict[str, Any])`, `get_job(...) -> dict[str, Any] | None`, `atomic_update(fields: dict[str, Any])`, `require_job(...) -> dict[str, Any]`. There is no type expressing that a job record *must* carry a `status: JobStatus` and `created_at: float`, *may* carry `terminal_reason: TerminalReason`, `completed_at`, `message`, `result`, `progress`, etc. The required-status invariant is enforced only by `require_job_status` reading `job.get("status")` (an `Any`) at one call site; `_job_eviction_timestamp_locked` (108) and `_clear_expired_heavy_objects_locked` (155) re-do `job.get("status") == "running"`/`"completed"` with bare literals, none type-checked. The seven `create_job` call sites (optimiser.py:254, _optimiser_service.py:2572/2923/2980, _train_service.py:436, _explore_service.py:561, modelling) each hand-build the dict with literal `"status": "running"` keys; a typo (`"staus"`) produces a job with NO status that passes `create_job` and only explodes later in `require_job_status`. This is the root primitive-obsession that all the other status findings (NodeResult, ExecutionMetricsPayload, terminal_reason mismatches catalogued in 02-findings #62) grow out of.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce a typed record for the job — minimally a `TypedDict` with `Required[]`/`NotRequired[]` (e.g. `class JobRecord(TypedDict): status: JobStatus; created_at: float; terminal_reason: NotRequired[TerminalReason]; completed_at: NotRequired[float]; ...`) so `create_job(initial: JobRecord)` and `get_job(...) -> JobRecord | None` give key/type checking at every call site for free, or (stronger) a frozen dataclass `Job` with the heavy/lightweight split modelled explicitly and `atomic_update` taking a typed patch. Either way, `status` becomes `JobStatus` not `Any`, the seven construction sites get checked, and the `job.get("status") == "running"` literals become `record["status"] is JobStatus.RUNNING`.

findings.location: src/haute/schemas.py:229-244 (NodeResult); constructed in src/haute/executor.py:1167-1204 (error shape) and 1189-1241 (ok shape)
findings.severity: high — a single flat optional-everywhere model conflates two mutually-exclusive result shapes (ok / error); contradictory records like status='ok' with error set, or status='error' carrying row_count/preview, are freely constructible and cross the API boundary, and every consumer must defensively re-check `status` to know which fields are meaningful
findings.title: NodeResult makes contradictory ok/error states representable (status: str + all-optional payload)
findings.description: `NodeResult` flattens an OK result and an ERROR result into one model where `status: str` (not even a Literal) gates which fields are meaningful, and every distinguishing field is optional/defaulted. The executor itself builds it in two disjoint shapes — error: `NodeResult(status="error", error=..., error_line=...)` (1167) leaving `row_count=0, columns=[], preview=[]`; ok: `NodeResult(status="ok", row_count=len(df), columns=..., preview=...)` (1227) leaving `error=None`. Nothing in the type prevents `NodeResult(status="ok", error="boom")` or `NodeResult(status="error", row_count=999, preview=[...])`; the line-1249 consumer must re-derive intent via `r.status == "error"`, and the frontend (api/types.ts) re-declares the same loose shape. The `status: str` also admits any string (e.g. `"OK"`, `"failed"`) — only convention keeps it to `{"ok","error"}`.
findings.recommended_design: Two complementary changes. (1) At minimum make `status: Literal["ok", "error"]` so the vocabulary is closed. (2) Better: model the sum type — `NodeOk(BaseModel)` (row_count, columns, available_columns, preview*, schema_warnings; no error fields) and `NodeError(BaseModel)` (error: str, error_line: int | None; no preview/columns), with `NodeResult = Annotated[NodeOk | NodeError, Field(discriminator="status")]` using a Pydantic discriminated union keyed on a `status` Literal per arm. Then an ok result cannot carry an error string and vice-versa — the illegal states stop being representable and consumers branch on the union, not a re-checked bare string.

findings.severity: medium — the status/terminal-reason fields that the GUI keys memory-diagnostic logic off (see 02-findings frontend memory-limited branches) are untyped strings even though exact enums exist; a wrong/typo'd reason serialises silently and the consumer's `terminal_reason === 'memory_limited'` comparison just quietly fails to match
findings.title: ExecutionMetricsPayload.status and .terminal_reason are bare str|None despite JobStatus / TerminalReason existing
findings.description: `ExecutionMetricsPayload` carries `status: str | None` (200) and `terminal_reason: str | None` (201). These are exactly the `JobStatus` and `TerminalReason` vocabularies — the publisher in `_job_lifecycle.py` even calls `context.metrics_payload(status=RUNNING_STATUS, terminal_reason=None)` (80-84) with a value drawn from the lifecycle status constants, and the terminal-write path stamps `terminal_reason=to` where `to: TerminalReason`. By widening to `str` at the schema boundary the type system stops verifying that what gets serialised is a real status/reason; any string (including a stale or misspelled one) validates. The frontend then does equality checks like `terminal_reason === 'memory_limited'`, which silently no-ops on drift rather than failing loudly — precisely the brittleness the surrounding memory-diagnostic findings describe.
findings.recommended_design: Type the fields with the existing closed vocabularies: `status: JobStatus | None` and `terminal_reason: TerminalReason | None` (importing the Literals, or the StrEnum from the consolidation in finding 1). Pydantic will then reject out-of-vocabulary values at validation time and `metrics_payload(...)` callers get checked at the call site. If a genuinely-open 'free text' status is ever needed it should be a separate explicitly-named field, not a widening of this one.

findings.severity: medium — the optimistic-concurrency guard that prevents a timeout/late write from clobbering a completed job is keyed on a bare `str`; a mistyped expected_status never equals any stored status, so the guard silently skips every update and returns None, and the caller's race-handling path fires unconditionally with no error
findings.title: Optimistic-concurrency `expected_status` guard is a bare str, not JobStatus
findings.description: The compare-and-set guard parameter is `expected_status: str | None` on `atomic_update` (387), `atomic_update_if_heavy_present` (431), and `JobLifecycle.transition` (112). The guard is load-bearing: `if old.get("status") != expected_status: return None` is what stops a timeout from overwriting a job that already completed (per the docstring at 403-406). Because the parameter is an unconstrained string, passing a value that is not a real `JobStatus` (a typo, or a constant that drifted from the lifecycle set per finding 1) compares unequal to every stored status, so the update is *always* skipped and `None` is returned — the very failure mode the guard exists to prevent, now triggered silently by a type error the compiler would have caught.
findings.recommended_design: Type the parameter `expected_status: JobStatus | None` (Literal or StrEnum). Every call site passing a status constant is then checked, and an out-of-vocabulary value is a compile error rather than a silent always-skip. This converts a runtime-only invariant ('expected_status must be a real status or the guard misbehaves') into a type-level guarantee.

findings.type_name: artifact handle (dict[str, Any]) + ArtifactCleaner registry keyed on str 'kind'
findings.severity: medium — artifact handles are untyped dicts probed at cleanup time with isinstance/get; a handle with a missing/misspelled 'kind' or absent 'directory'/'path' is fully constructible and surfaces only as a warning-logged skipped cleanup (leaked files), never a construction-time error
findings.title: Artifact handles are untyped dicts and cleaner registry is keyed on a bare 'kind' string
findings.description: `register_artifact_cleaner(kind: str, ...)` (40) registers cleanup hooks in a `dict[str, ArtifactCleaner]` keyed by an arbitrary string, and `_cleanup_artifact_handles` (121-150) reconstructs handle semantics entirely at runtime: `handles = job.get("artifact_handles")`; `if not isinstance(handles, dict)`; per handle `if not isinstance(handle, dict)`, `kind = handle.get("kind")`, `cleaner = _ARTIFACT_CLEANERS.get(kind) if isinstance(kind, str) else None`, then path via `handle.get("directory") or handle.get("path")`. Nothing types a handle as `{kind: <known kind>, directory|path: str}`; a producer can store a handle with no `kind`, an unknown `kind`, or neither path key, and the only feedback is a `job_artifact_cleanup_unknown_handle_kind` warning while the on-disk artifact silently leaks. The set of valid kinds is open and unvalidated at registration.
findings.recommended_design: Model the handle as a typed structure — a `TypedDict ArtifactHandle { kind: ArtifactKind; directory: NotRequired[str]; path: NotRequired[str] }` (or a small frozen dataclass), where `ArtifactKind` is a Literal/StrEnum of the registered kinds, and store `artifact_handles: dict[str, ArtifactHandle]` on the (now typed, per finding 2) job record. Have `register_artifact_cleaner` take `kind: ArtifactKind` so registration is checked against the closed set. The cleanup loop then drops the `isinstance`/`get` probing and the 'unknown kind' branch becomes unreachable-by-construction rather than a logged leak.

findings.location: src/haute/routes/_job_store.py:30-32, 196-198 (heavy-object sentinel/bookkeeping keys), 524-531 (clear_result_data) — keys live inside the same flat job dict[str, Any]
findings.type_name: JobStore heavy-object lifecycle bookkeeping keys (heavy_objects_expires_at / heavy_objects_cleared_at / heavy_objects_retention_seconds)
findings.severity: low-medium — engine-owned lifecycle bookkeeping is stored as magic string keys in the same untyped dict that holds caller-supplied fields (config, result, message...), so a caller passing a field of one of these reserved names corrupts eviction scheduling; the namespace collision is unrepresentable-by-type to detect
findings.title: Heavy-object lifecycle bookkeeping shares the job dict namespace with caller domain fields
findings.description: The job dict mixes two ownership domains in one flat `dict[str, Any]`: caller domain fields (`status`, `config`, `result`, `message`, `progress`, the heavy objects `solver`/`solve_result`/`quote_grid`/...) and JobStore-private lifecycle bookkeeping written as bare string keys — `_HEAVY_OBJECT_EXPIRES_AT_KEY = "heavy_objects_expires_at"` (32), and in `_clear_heavy_objects_locked` the injected `"heavy_objects_cleared_at"` / `"heavy_objects_retention_seconds"` (197-198). Because both share the namespace, a `create_job`/`update_job` caller that happens to pass a field named `heavy_objects_expires_at` (e.g. surfacing one in a status payload) directly perturbs the expiry the store computes in `_heavy_objects_expires_at` (202-208), and the heavy-key tuple `_HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS` (30-31) being a list of bare strings means the same collision risk applies to the heavy payload keys. The store's invariants about its own bookkeeping are not encapsulated away from caller-controlled keys.
findings.recommended_design: Separate the two domains structurally. Promote the job record to a typed object (finding 2) with an explicit, non-dict-keyed sub-structure for lifecycle bookkeeping — e.g. a `HeavyObjectPolicy` dataclass (`expires_at: float | None`, `cleared_at: float | None`, `retention_seconds: int`) held in a dedicated field, kept in a side-table (`dict[job_id, HeavyObjectPolicy]` like the existing `_running_activity_at`/`_heavy_object_timers`), so caller fields and engine bookkeeping can never collide in one namespace. Heavy-object key membership should likewise be a typed/closed set rather than a bare-string tuple compared against arbitrary caller keys.

findings.title: Model flavour is stringly-typed and its valid set is duplicated across 4 independent sites
findings.severity: high
findings.description: The scoring flavour is passed as a bare `str` through every scoring surface (`score_frame(flavor: str)`, `_score_eager_unified`, `_score_batched_unified`, `_prepare_predict_frame(flavor='pyfunc')`, `ScoringModel.flavor: str = 'pyfunc'`). The authoritative set of legal values is encoded FOUR separate times with no shared source of truth: (1) `_SUPPORTED_FLAVORS = frozenset({'catboost','pyfunc','rustystats'})` (_model_scorer.py:32); (2) the membership check + error message in `score_frame` (:779-785); (3) a *second*, independently hard-coded check `if flavor not in ('catboost','pyfunc')` plus the `rustystats` early-return in `_prepare_predict_frame` (_mlflow_io.py:1078-1085); (4) the constructor `_flavor_from_artifact` (_mlflow_io.py:64-76) which maps extensions to the flavour strings. Each branch (`flavor == 'catboost'`, `== 'rustystats'`, `== 'pyfunc'`) is a literal string compared by eye. Nothing prevents constructing a `ScoringModel(flavor='catbost')` (typo) — the type checker is blind, and the failure only surfaces deep in `score_frame`/`_prepare_predict_frame` as a runtime `ConfigError`/`ValueError`. Adding a new flavour requires editing all four sites and there is no compiler signal if one is missed (e.g. `_prepare_predict_frame`'s `('catboost','pyfunc')` tuple is a known divergence risk from `_SUPPORTED_FLAVORS`). This is squarely against the project's own established pattern: `NodeType`, `ExecutionProfile`, `SourceFormat`, `ChunkCapabilityKind`, `_CheckpointAction` are all `StrEnum`s.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `class ModelFlavor(StrEnum): CATBOOST='catboost'; PYFUNC='pyfunc'; RUSTYSTATS='rustystats'` in `_mlflow_io.py` (or a shared modelling types module). Type every flavour parameter and `ScoringModel.flavor` as `ModelFlavor`. Replace `_SUPPORTED_FLAVORS` with `frozenset(ModelFlavor)` (or just iterate the enum). Make `_prepare_predict_frame` dispatch with `match flavor:` / `if flavor is ModelFlavor.RUSTYSTATS` so a missing case is a single source of truth, and drop the independently-spelled `('catboost','pyfunc')` tuple. Because `StrEnum` members compare equal to their string value, JSON/config reads (`_flavor_from_artifact`, `cfg.get(...)`) can coerce via `ModelFlavor(raw)` at the boundary — which then *fails loudly at the edge* on an unknown value instead of silently flowing a bad string inward. This removes the entire class of typo/desync bugs and makes 'add a flavour' a single-enum-plus-exhaustive-match change.

findings.type_name: task — bare `str` in scorer & algorithms vs existing `Task = Literal['classification','regression']`
findings.title: `task` is `str` across the scorer/algorithm surface even though a `Task` literal alias already exists and is used elsewhere
findings.severity: high
findings.description: `_feature_contract.py:29` defines `Task = Literal['classification','regression']` and `_signature.py:36` already types its parameter as `Literal['classification','regression']`. Yet the entire scoring/training hot path types `task` as a bare `str`: `score_frame(task: str = 'regression')`, `_score_eager_unified`, `_score_batched_unified`, `_run_score_pipeline`, `ModelScorer.__init__(task: str)`, `BaseAlgorithm.fit(task: str)`, `CatBoostAlgorithm.fit`, `GLMAlgorithm.fit`, and `resolve_loss_function(task: str)`. Seven modules then branch on `task == 'classification'` / `task == 'regression'` (grep-confirmed: `_mlflow_io`, `_model_scorer`, `_training_job`, `_algorithms`, `_model_explainability`, `_mlflow_log`, `_signature`). Because the parameter is `str`, a typo like `task='regresion'` type-checks and silently routes through the *else* arm (e.g. in `score_frame` it skips the `_proba` column; in `resolve_loss_function` it selects `CLASSIFICATION_LOSSES` for any non-'regression' string — line 231 `valid = REGRESSION_LOSSES if task == 'regression' else CLASSIFICATION_LOSSES`, so 'regresion' is silently treated as classification). The `Task` alias is already the right abstraction; it is simply not threaded through.
findings.recommended_design: Promote the existing `Task` literal to a shared location (e.g. a small `haute/modelling/_types.py` or reuse the one in `_feature_contract.py`) and annotate every `task` parameter and `ScoringModel`/`ModelScorer` field with `Task`. Optionally upgrade to `class Task(StrEnum)` for richer call-sites; the `Literal` alone already makes mypy/pyright reject the typo at every call boundary. In `resolve_loss_function`, branch on the exhaustive literal so a 4th task value would be a type error, and replace the `else` fallthrough with an explicit `task == 'classification'` check so a non-'regression' string can never be silently misclassified.

findings.title: ScoringModel is a 'uniform interface' carrier with mutable public fields — its invariants (flavour ∈ supported set, feature ordering, cat ⊆ features) can be broken after construction
findings.severity: medium
findings.description: `ScoringModel` is the central uniform-interface object the whole scoring layer trusts: `_validate_features` keys its cache on `(id(model), tuple(model.feature_names), frozenset(model.cat_feature_names))` (_model_scorer.py:119-124) and CatBoost positional categorical-index alignment depends on `feature_names` ordering being exactly training order. Yet `feature_names: list[str]`, `cat_feature_names: frozenset[str]`, and `flavor: str` are plain writable attributes (it uses `__slots__` but is not frozen and exposes no read-only views). Any code holding a cached/shared `ScoringModel` (these are cached in `_model_cache` and shared across threads — see the eviction-cascade machinery) can do `model.feature_names.append('x')` or `model.flavor = 'pyfunc'` and (a) silently desync the feature-validation cache from reality (the cache key snapshots a tuple at call time, so a later in-place `list.append` is invisible until the next key recompute), and (b) violate the documented invariant that `flavor` is one of the supported dispatch targets. There is also no construction-time guarantee that `cat_feature_names ⊆ set(feature_names)`; a stray cat name simply never matches.
findings.recommended_design: Make `ScoringModel` an immutable value object: `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` (or keep the hand-written class but store `feature_names` as a `tuple[str, ...]` and validate in `__post_init__`/`__init__`). Type `flavor: ModelFlavor` (per the flavour-enum finding) so an illegal flavour is unconstructable. Validate the cross-field invariant `cat_feature_names <= set(feature_names)` at construction and raise a named error otherwise — turning the silent 'cat name never matches' failure into a loud one. With `feature_names` as a tuple, the cache key derivation is honestly stable and `list.append`-style mutation is impossible.

findings.location: src/haute/modelling/_feature_contract.py:53-64 (FeatureContract); construction at :96-134; consumed by hash at :91-93, 116-124
findings.title: FeatureContract is `frozen=True` but stores mutable list/dict fields, so its content-hash invariant can be silently desynced by in-place mutation
findings.severity: medium
findings.description: `FeatureContract` is documented as an 'Immutable record' and uses `@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)`, but `frozen=True` only blocks *attribute rebinding* — it does nothing about mutation of the contained containers. The fields `features: list[str]`, `feature_types: dict[str,str]`, `categorical_features: list[str]`, `categorical_levels: dict[str, list[str|None]]` are all mutable, and the central invariant of the type is that `contract_hash == sha256(canonical(all other fields))`. A holder can do `contract.features.append('leaked')` or `contract.categorical_levels['x'].append('y')` and the object now carries a `contract_hash` that no longer matches its own content, which is exactly the corruption `load_contract(verify_hash=True)` exists to catch on disk — but the in-memory object provides no such protection. Because `load_contract_cached` returns a *process-wide shared* instance across threads (the docstring says 'shared across callers and threads — treat it as immutable'), a single accidental in-place mutation poisons the contract for every concurrent scorer, and `assert_contracts_match` (which compares field-by-field) would then compare against mutated state. The immutability is by-convention only.
findings.recommended_design: Make the contents genuinely immutable so the hash invariant is structurally guaranteed: store `features`/`categorical_features` as `tuple[str, ...]`, `feature_types` as an immutable mapping (e.g. wrap in `types.MappingProxyType` or a frozen mapping), and `categorical_levels` as `Mapping[str, tuple[str|None, ...]]`. Keep `build_contract`/`load_contract` accepting plain lists/dicts at the boundary and freezing on the way in (they already copy). With frozen contents, `contract_hash` cannot drift from content for the lifetime of the object, eliminating the 'shared mutable contract' hazard entirely and letting the on-disk `verify_hash` be the *only* place corruption can enter.

findings.title: CatBoost loss names are validated at runtime from bare string sets instead of being a typed closed union
findings.severity: medium
findings.description: `REGRESSION_LOSSES = {'RMSE','MAE','Poisson','Tweedie'}` and `CLASSIFICATION_LOSSES = {'Logloss','CrossEntropy'}` are bare `set[str]` module constants, and `resolve_loss_function(loss_name: str, task: str, ...)` validates membership purely at runtime (raising `ValueError` on a miss). The legal-loss vocabulary is therefore invisible to the type system: callers pass an arbitrary `str`, and the only signal that 'RMS' (typo) or 'logloss' (wrong case) is invalid is a runtime exception during training-config assembly. Combined with the `task: str` weakness above, the selector at line 231 (`valid = REGRESSION_LOSSES if task == 'regression' else CLASSIFICATION_LOSSES`) means a bad `task` value silently changes *which* loss set is considered valid. The valid set is small, closed, and known at authoring time — a textbook candidate for a literal union / enum.
findings.recommended_design: Define `RegressionLoss = Literal['RMSE','MAE','Poisson','Tweedie']` and `ClassificationLoss = Literal['Logloss','CrossEntropy']` (or `StrEnum`s), derive the runtime sets from them (`frozenset(get_args(RegressionLoss))`) so there is a single source of truth, and type `resolve_loss_function(loss_name: RegressionLoss | ClassificationLoss | None, task: Task, ...)`. The runtime check stays as a belt-and-braces guard for config-file inputs, but in-code callers now get a compile-time error for an unknown loss, and the regression/classification split is enforced by `Task` being a closed union.

findings.type_name: GLM family / link — bare `str` read from an untyped `params: dict[str, Any]`
findings.title: GLM `family` and `link` are stringly-typed and pulled from an untyped params dict, with behaviour-changing string equality (`family == 'tweedie'`) unguarded by the type system
findings.severity: medium
findings.description: The GLM distribution `family` and `link` flow as bare `str` (`_build_glm_builder_kwargs(family: str, link: str | None)`), read out of an opaque `params: dict[str, Any]` in `GLMAlgorithm.fit` via `params.get('family', 'gaussian')` / `params.get('link') or None`. Behaviour branches on exact string equality — `if family == 'tweedie': kwargs['var_power'] = var_power` (line 135) — so a miscapitalised or misspelled `family` ('Tweedie', 'tweedy') silently skips the `var_power` wiring and is forwarded verbatim to `rs.glm_dict`, where it either errors cryptically or (worse) is interpreted differently than intended. There is no enumeration of supported families/links anywhere in the Python layer, so neither the type checker nor a reader can see the legal vocabulary, and the train-config surface accepts any string. This is the GLM analogue of the CatBoost-loss issue and the flavour issue.
findings.recommended_design: Introduce `GLMFamily = Literal['gaussian','poisson','gamma','tweedie', ...]` and `GLMLink = Literal[...]` (enumerate against what RustyStats actually accepts) and type `_build_glm_builder_kwargs(family: GLMFamily, link: GLMLink | None)`. Validate/coerce `params['family']`/`params['link']` to these at the `fit` boundary (the one place untyped config becomes typed) so an unknown family fails loudly there rather than inside the Rust layer, and so the `family == 'tweedie'` branch is checked against a closed set. This makes the supported-distribution set discoverable and the `var_power` coupling robust to typos.

findings.location: src/haute/_model_scorer.py:1015-1019 (source_type, version) and 980-989 docstring; consumed in _mlflow_io.load_mlflow_model:852-875
findings.title: `source_type` ('run' | 'registered') and `version` ('latest' | digits) are stringly-typed across the MLflow loading surface
findings.severity: low
findings.description: `ModelScorer.__init__(source_type: str, version: str = 'latest')` and `load_mlflow_model(source_type: str, ...)` accept bare strings whose only legal values are `'run'`/`'registered'` (source_type) and `'latest'` or a version-number string (version). `load_mlflow_model` branches on `source_type == 'run'` (line 893) and the docstrings enumerate the two values, but nothing in the type system enforces them: `source_type='registerd'` type-checks and would fall into the non-'run' path, attempting a registered-model lookup with an empty `registered_model`. The required *companion* field also differs by `source_type` (run_id for 'run', registered_model for 'registered'), so this is also a latent illegal-states issue — a `ModelScorer(source_type='run')` with empty `run_id` and a populated `registered_model` is representable and meaningless.
findings.recommended_design: Type `source_type` as `Literal['run','registered']` (or a `ModelSource` StrEnum). For the stronger fix, model the source as a small tagged union so the run-vs-registered companion fields cannot be mismatched — e.g. `RunSource(run_id: str, artifact_path: str)` vs `RegisteredSource(name: str, version: str | Literal['latest'])` — making 'run source with no run_id' unrepresentable. At minimum the literal on `source_type` catches the typo and the wrong-path-with-empty-id failure mode.

findings.title: ScoreWriteProjection is already well-designed (frozen, slots, frozenset fields, documented sentinel) — no change recommended
findings.severity: info
findings.description: Recording the positive: `ScoreWriteProjection` is an exemplary small value object for this codebase. It is `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`; its collection fields are `frozenset[str]` (immutable, no in-place mutation hazard like the ScoringModel/FeatureContract findings above); the `passthrough_columns: frozenset[str] | None = None` sentinel is explicitly documented ('None passthrough means preserve the full scored input; a concrete set means write exactly those'), so the `Optional` here encodes a genuine two-state choice rather than hiding a required invariant. The defaults (`frozenset()` for optional/required) are correct empty-set identities. No illegal state is constructible. I reviewed it specifically because the surface brief flags optional-everywhere and encapsulation risks — this type does NOT exhibit them and should be left as-is (and is a good template for tightening ScoringModel/FeatureContract).
findings.recommended_design: No change. Use as the reference pattern (frozen + slots + frozenset/tuple fields + a single documented sentinel) when tightening `ScoringModel` and `FeatureContract` per the other findings.
